Founded in 1997 with roots in Javalobby, DZone reaches millions of developers each month with articles, tutorials, research guides, and Refcards covering topics including cloud architecture, Java, JavaScript, microservices, containers, data, DevOps, AI, and more.

providers.name: Hornet
providers.description: Hornet is a queer social networking platform operated by Queer Networks, Inc., serving the global LGBTQ+ community with more than 100 million users worldwide. The Hornet app combines profiles, feeds, live video, one-on-one video chat, messaging, and location-based discovery into a privacy-first digital home for gay men and the broader queer community. Backed by 500 Global (and previously part of BlueCity Holdings), Hornet operates as a consumer social/media company rather than an API provider — it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDKs — so this API Evangelist profile captures the company's public identity, policy surface, and domain-security posture rather than developer artifacts. Hornet is number one in several key markets including France, Brazil, Turkey, and Taiwan, and monetizes through premium subscriptions and queer-audience advertising.

providers.name: BuzzFeed
providers.description: BuzzFeed Inc. is a digital media company founded in 2006 and headquartered in New York City, best known for its viral entertainment, quizzes, pop-culture coverage, and commerce content. The company operates a portfolio of brands including the flagship BuzzFeed site, the news operation HuffPost, and the food brand Tasty, and produces video, podcasts, and shoppable content across web and social platforms. BuzzFeed is a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: BZFD) and monetizes through advertising, brand partnerships, and commerce. It does not publish a general-purpose public developer API program; its public machine-readable surface consists of content syndication (RSS feeds), an advertising/partnerships business, and a security.txt vulnerability-disclosure program via HackerOne. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from an a16z portfolio lead and enriched with the provider's real public surface.

providers.name: Shred Video
providers.description: Shred Video automates cinematic video and photo production for adventure tourism operators. Using LiDAR, GPS, smart camera technology, and proprietary algorithms, the platform automatically captures, edits, and delivers finished cinematic videos and photos to a customer's phone within seconds of an activity. It serves adventure tour operators such as skydiving centers, bungy jumping and giant swing operators, river rafting outfitters, and paragliding services, with documented clients including Skydive Utah and AJ Hackett locations in Australia and Singapore. Shred Video is a Y Combinator portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the company operates a marketing and demo-request website but publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation portal, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Spotter
providers.description: Spotter is a creator-economy platform that invests in YouTube creators through capital, catalog licensing, and brand partnerships, and connects brands with top long-form YouTube creators for marketing and content opportunities. Its Spotter Studio product provides AI-assisted tooling that helps creators plan, ideate, and optimize their content and titles. The company reports more than $1 billion invested in creators and over 43 billion monthly views across a network that includes creators such as MrBeast, Critical Role, and Sam and Colby. Spotter is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund. Spotter publishes no public developer API: contract discovery on 2026-08-13 found no OpenAPI, GraphQL SDL, AsyncAPI, MCP server or A2A agent card on any Spotter host, and the Spotter Studio application backends return 503 to anonymous callers. Spotter Studio is a consumer of the YouTube Data and Analytics APIs via Google OAuth, not a provider of one.

providers.name: The Atavist
providers.description: The Atavist is a pioneering digital longform-storytelling brand founded in 2009 by Evan Ratliff, Jefferson Rabb, and Nicholas Thompson. It comprises The Atavist Magazine, which publishes one immersive work of narrative nonfiction each month and has earned National Magazine Award and Emmy recognition, and the Atavist multimedia publishing platform for building rich, media-driven stories. Automattic (the company behind WordPress.com) acquired both the magazine and the platform in 2018; the platform's storytelling features were folded into WordPress.com and the magazine now runs on Newspack by Automattic. The Atavist exposes no public developer API or documented developer program — it is a reader-facing publication at magazine.atavist.com.

providers.name: TuneCore
providers.description: TuneCore is a Brooklyn, New York based independent music distribution and publishing administration company founded in 2006 (as YourTunes, Inc., rebranded TuneCore in 2008) and acquired by French music company Believe in 2015. TuneCore lets self-releasing artists and labels deliver recorded music to 150+ digital stores and streaming services — Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon Music, YouTube Music, TikTok, Tidal, Deezer, Beatport, and others — while retaining 100% of their rights and master ownership, in exchange for a flat annual distribution fee starting at $24.99/year for unlimited releases. TuneCore Publishing Administration registers compositions with performance rights organizations, mechanical rights societies, and digital service providers worldwide to collect songwriter royalties, sync, and neighboring rights income. Additional services include the TuneCore Accelerator artist development program, TuneCore Social (monetization on TikTok, Reels, and Shorts), TuneCore Direct Advance (royalty-backed capital, powered by RoyFi), mastering, and Splits for collaborator revenue sharing. TuneCore operates across 5 continents with local teams in 15+ countries through Believe's global network. There is no current public TuneCore developer API, SDK, or partner portal — an earlier white-label REST/XML "TuneCore Direct" partner API existed circa 2008-2012 (with a community Ruby gem `tunecore_direct`) but is no longer actively documented or promoted. TuneCore's public-facing surface is the artist web app at web.tunecore.com and the support/help center; any current B2B integrations run through Believe's enterprise partnerships.

providers.name: Watch Club
providers.description: Watch Club is a mobile streaming and social platform for young adults, built around original coming-of-age teen drama series that viewers watch and then discuss with other fans through polls, episode reactions, and community threads. Its first original series, RETURN OFFER, launches February 2026, with a slate of additional YA series in development. The app is available on iOS and is operated by Kino Technologies Inc. Watch Club is a GV (Google Ventures) portfolio company in the consumer sector; it publishes no public developer API surface as of this profile.

providers.name: Mind Candy, Moshi
providers.description: Mind Candy Ltd is a London-based children's media and technology company, originally known for the Moshi Monsters online game and now operating Moshi, an award-winning children's app for sleep, relaxation and learning. Moshi offers hundreds of hours of bedtime stories, sleep sounds, music, white noise and educational activities delivered through iOS and Android consumer apps. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network. Moshi is a direct-to-consumer subscription product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Gen.G
providers.description: Gen.G is a global esports organization founded in 2017 (originally KSV eSports) that connects the United States and Asia, operating from Los Angeles, Seoul, and Shanghai. It fields professional teams across League of Legends, Valorant, PUBG, Counter-Strike 2, Rocket League, Fortnite, Brawl Stars, Honor of Kings, Mobile Legends, NBA 2K, Overwatch, Rainbow Six Siege, and EA FC, and runs a youth esports academy program alongside merchandise and fan-engagement businesses. Backed by Canaan Partners among other investors, Gen.G was valued at roughly $250 million as of 2022. It is a consumer esports brand and merchandise operator with a Shopify-based storefront; it publishes no public developer API, so this profile carries company identity only.

providers.name: Rephrase.ai
providers.description: Rephrase.ai is a Bengaluru-based generative-AI startup whose text-to-video platform, Rephrase Studio, turns plain text scripts into videos of digital human avatars ("actors") that speak the script with lip-synced, natural voices. It exposed a Rephrase Studio API for programmatic video generation (list actors and voices, create and export videos, poll video status) secured with OAuth2 bearer tokens. Backed by Techstars, Rephrase.ai was acquired by Adobe in November 2023 and its technology folded into Adobe's video and generative-AI offerings; the standalone product hosts have since been decommissioned, though the legacy API reference remains hosted on ReadMe. This profile is maintained by API Evangelist for historical and enrichment purposes.

providers.name: BabyCenter
providers.description: BabyCenter is an online pregnancy and parenting media company founded in 1997 and operated today by Everyday Health Group, a division of Ziff Davis. It provides medically reviewed information and interactive tools covering conception, pregnancy, birth, and early childhood development, and publishes the widely used "My Pregnancy & Baby Today" mobile app for iOS and Android used by hundreds of millions of expecting and new parents worldwide. BabyCenter operates as a content and community destination rather than an API platform: it does not publish a public developer program, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or hosted API, and its verified GitHub organization contains only forked iOS libraries. This API Evangelist profile captures the company's public operational surface — domain security posture, a live RFC 9116 security.txt with a Ziff Davis Bugcrowd vulnerability disclosure program, and its editorial/legal properties.

providers.name: TREBEL Music
providers.description: TREBEL Music (operated by M&M Media, Inc.) is an advertising-sponsored, legally licensed music download and streaming service that lets people download and listen to music offline at no cost. Founded in 2014 by Gary Mekikian, Corey Jones and Luis Soto Durazo and headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut with offices in Mexico City, Jakarta, Bogota, Los Angeles and Miami, TREBEL licenses catalog from Universal Music Group, Sony Music Entertainment, Warner Music Group and independent labels, and monetizes through digital advertising, branded experiences, virtual goods and a TREBEL Max tier rather than a conventional paid subscription. TREBEL is a consumer mobile product distributed through the Apple App Store, Google Play and Huawei AppGallery; it publishes no public developer program, API reference, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: TT Labs
providers.description: TT Labs is the company behind VideoPixie, a freelance marketplace that connects clients with professional video creators — videographers, video editors, directors, animators, and motion designers — available for hire. Clients post a project brief in about five minutes and receive competitive bids from vetted creators, then choose a creator based on portfolio and price. VideoPixie serves crowdfunding and Kickstarter videos, product and explainer videos, game trailers, wedding videography, screencasts, and full production campaigns, with example budgets ranging from a few hundred to tens of thousands of dollars. Backed by 500 Global, VideoPixie is a customer-facing marketplace web application (AngularJS) and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or client SDKs.

providers.name: Cosm
providers.description: Cosm is a Los Angeles-based immersive technology, media and entertainment company formed in 2020 from the merger of LiveLike VR (now Cosm Immersive) and C360, followed by the acquisition of planetarium pioneers Evans & Sutherland and Spitz. It operates three lines: Cosm Tech (the CX System LED dome, Digistar planetarium software, and end-to-end immersive display systems sold to planetariums, museums and attractions), Cosm Media (immersive content production and licensing through Cosm Studios) and Cosm Venues (the "Shared Reality" experiential venues in Los Angeles and Dallas, with Atlanta, Detroit and Cleveland following). Cosm sells and operates systems and venues rather than a developer platform: it publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable specification. The one API it markets — the Digistar scripting/automation interface, advertised as "the most fully featured API across the planetarium industry" — is documented only inside the customer support portal at partners.cosm.com, which requires a login.

providers.name: Lil Snack
providers.description: Lil Snack is a Manhattan Beach, California games company, founded in 2024, that builds "snackable" daily games and party games — short pop-culture puzzle, word, and trivia titles that refresh every day. It runs its own consumer destination at lilsnack.com (Clue Daily, Scattergories Daily, Swap, DownWords, Pickle, Lite Brite Daily, Wheel of Fortune TODAY, Quiz Climb, Venn, Chain, and more) and also powers games embedded inside partner consumer platforms, citing BuzzFeed, FOX, Hasbro, the Los Angeles Times, Netflix, Peacock, Prime Gaming, Reddit, and Sony. The company reports 40M+ games played and 10M+ players all-time, and monetizes through platform partnerships, sponsorships, and brand licensing. As of this profile Lil Snack publishes NO public developer surface — no API, no documentation portal, no SDKs, no public GitHub organization, and no /.well-known documents; its partner game integrations are arranged through business development rather than self-serve APIs. This API Evangelist profile therefore captures verified company identity, web properties, and probed domain-security posture only.

providers.name: 9GAG
providers.description: 9GAG is a Hong Kong-based global entertainment platform founded in 2008 with the mission to "make the world happier." It is one of the largest meme and user-generated humor communities on the internet, distributing funny images, GIFs, and videos across its website and iOS/Android apps to an audience of 150-200 million people and billions of monthly video views. 9GAG operates consumer-facing products (the 9GAG feed, 9GAG Pro subscription, and related community features) rather than a public developer API program; it was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a venture-backed company (500 Global, Y Combinator, Freestyle Capital, True Ventures, First Round Capital, Greycroft) and has been enriched with its real public web, policy, and security surfaces. No official public API or developer portal is published as of this enrichment; the community libraries that exist are unofficial and reverse-engineered.

providers.name: Girlboss
providers.description: Girlboss is a community and media brand for ambitious women, positioned as a navigator for the future of work — created to spark the thrill of possibility and to inspire and inform so members can find success on their own terms. Founded by Sophia Amoruso (author of #GIRLBOSS and founder of Nasty Gal), Girlboss grew from editorial content, newsletters, and the Girlboss Rally events into a community brand. Today girlboss.com runs as a Shopify-hosted storefront and brand site. Girlboss was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners; it publishes no first-party developer API, so this profile captures its public web, policy, and agent-facing (llms.txt / well-known) surface rather than an API.

providers.name: Herb
providers.description: Herb (herb.co) is a leading digital media and e-commerce platform dedicated to cannabis culture, education, and lifestyle. It publishes cannabis news, strain databases, product reviews, dispensary and brand guides, deals, recipes, and city-level legalization guides, and operates the "Herb Agency" offering branding and marketing services to cannabis companies. The consumer site is built on Gatsby (React) with a GraphQL data layer, Algolia search, and a Firebase/serverless backend hosted on Netlify. Herb is backed by Bullpen Capital and was added to the API Evangelist network from that portfolio; the company exposes no public developer API program at this time, so this profile captures its published web, content, and discovery surface (llms.txt, domain security posture, and identity/link properties) rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: MediaBeacon
providers.description: MediaBeacon is a Digital Asset Management (DAM) platform from Esko with a highly flexible architecture and open APIs that enable integration into many products. Its APIs support hands-off data transfer between services, reducing human intervention and enabling workflow automation.

providers.name: Pratilipi
providers.description: Pratilipi is India's largest digital storytelling platform, democratizing story creation and consumption across languages, formats, and boundaries. Built by Nasadiya Technologies Private Limited and headquartered in Bangalore, it lets more than 300,000 self-published writers reach roughly 25 million monthly readers across twelve Indian languages (Hindi, Gujarati, Marathi, Bengali, English, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Punjabi, Urdu, and Odia). The ecosystem spans Pratilipi Literature, Pratilipi FM (audio books, podcasts, and folk songs), Pratilipi Comics (the largest Hindi online comic platform), Westland Publications, and IVM Podcasts, carrying a story "from someone's draft to someone's screen." Pratilipi does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures the company's identity, web properties, and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Booko
providers.description: Booko is an Australian book, eBook, audiobook, DVD, music and collectibles price-comparison service operating since 2007. It aggregates new and used prices across many online retailers and regions, calculates shipping, and converts international prices to the shopper's local currency to surface the cheapest place to buy a title. Booko also offers shopping lists with bundled shipping calculations, barcode scanning, reading lists, price alerts and notifications. It is a consumer-facing comparison site rather than a retailer or a public API provider, earning referral fees from partner shops (including Amazon Associates) when shoppers buy through its links. Booko is a solo developer-run product surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a Y Combinator portfolio company.

providers.name: CBS (Paramount Global)
providers.description: CBS is the flagship broadcast television network of Paramount Global (NASDAQ: PARA, PARAA). It encompasses CBS Entertainment, CBS News, CBS Sports, CBS Stations (owned and operated), and feeds Paramount+ streaming service. CBS does not publish a consumer developer portal. Partner, syndication, advertising, and distribution APIs are operated privately through Paramount Global's business development, ad sales, and affiliate operations teams.

providers.name: Qsic
providers.description: Qsic (styled QSIC) is an Australian-founded, AI-driven in-store audio and retail media platform, headquartered in Melbourne with a North American office in Dallas, Texas. The platform blends curated music, targeted audio advertising and store-level intelligence, deploying either over a retailer's existing speaker infrastructure or over premium smart speakers, and adapting playback to ambient conditions, dayparts and shopper behaviour. Qsic sells three connected products — In-Store Audio, Ads and Intelligence — and positions the combination as a way to turn physical stores into measurable retail media networks with store-level performance reporting and demand-side platform integration. Publicly reported deployments include 7-Eleven ("Gulp Radio"), Dollar General, Coles Liquor and Mecca. Qsic runs a live JSON API host at api.getqsic.com and a Vanta-hosted trust center, but publishes no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification as of this profile.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: SeekingAlpha
providers.description: Seeking Alpha is a crowd-sourced investment research and analysis platform for stock-market investors, providing breaking financial news, analyst articles, earnings-call transcripts, dividend and quant ratings, stock and ETF screeners, portfolio tracking, and subscription research services (Premium, Pro, and Alpha Picks). Backed by Accel and headquartered in Israel, it serves individual investors worldwide. Added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public first-party developer API is currently published.

providers.name: Showrunner
providers.description: Showrunner is an AI streaming and animation platform built by Fable Simulation (founded by Edward Saatchi) and billed as the "Netflix of AI." It lets users create and watch AI-generated serialized animated television shows across genres, acting as directors to write, produce, voice, and remix full episodes within simulated worlds such as Sim Francisco, alongside flagship series like Exit Valley. The platform is powered by Fable's proprietary SHOW-2 model and is delivered as a consumer iOS app and Discord community. Showrunner publishes no first-party developer API; its public site is a Wix-hosted marketing property that exposes the standard Wix Site MCP endpoint for agentic access to public site content.

providers.name: Xperi
providers.description: Xperi Inc. (NYSE: XPER) is an entertainment technology company whose licensed technologies power audio, video, and media discovery experiences across connected cars, consumer electronics, pay-TV, and streaming media platforms. Its brands include DTS immersive audio, HD Radio digital broadcast radio, IMAX Enhanced certification, and the TiVo video platform. Xperi ships its technologies to automakers, device makers, and video providers through commercial licensing and integration programs rather than a public developer API; no public developer portal or API documentation was found, though its TiVo engineering organization maintains an open-source presence on GitHub.

providers.name: All City Network
providers.description: ALLCITY Network (All City Network) is a sports media and podcasting company built on the tagline "Sports Over Everything." It operates a set of city-based sports networks — DNVR (Denver), PHNX (Phoenix), CHGO (Chicago), PHLY (Philadelphia), and DLLS (Dallas) — that produce team-focused podcasts, video shows, and written coverage of local professional and collegiate sports, alongside network-wide shows and NBA/NFL programming. The company reaches fans through audio and video podcasts, memberships, and a merchandise store. It is a Bullpen Capital portfolio company and is not an API provider; it publishes no developer portal, documentation, or API, so the API-specific artifacts of the enrichment pipeline are not applicable.

providers.name: Audible
providers.description: Audible is an Amazon-owned online audiobook, podcast, and spoken-word entertainment service. It sells and streams audiobooks, Audible Originals, and podcasts through membership plans and a la carte purchases, delivered via web, iOS, Android, Alexa, and Kindle apps. Audible does not operate a public developer program or documented API — its catalog, library, and playback endpoints are a private internal API consumed by its own first-party apps. Community projects (the mkb79/Audible Python library, audible-cli, and omarroth/audible.cr) reverse-engineer that internal API; none are first-party or officially supported. This profile catalogs Audible's public web, help, and legal surface plus the unofficial client ecosystem.

providers.name: Awa Studios
providers.description: AWA Studios (Artists, Writers & Artisans, Inc.) is a New York-based independent multimedia entertainment company founded in 2018 by comics-industry veterans, including former Marvel editor-in-chief Axel Alonso and former Marvel president Bill Jemas, with media executive Jon Miller as board chairman. AWA publishes original comic books and graphic novels across action, crime, horror, science fiction, and fantasy genres, built around a creator-owned business model that offers favorable terms to writers and artists. The company operates the "Upshot" imprint and a shared "Resistance Universe," runs a direct-to-consumer shop for print and digital titles, and develops film and television adaptations of its properties. AWA received seed-stage funding from Lightspeed Venture Partners in 2018. It is a media and entertainment company and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Blue Wire
providers.description: Blue Wire is a podcast network and monetization platform built for independent sports content creators, positioning itself as "The Monetization Engine for Sports Creators." The company provides sales, marketing, distribution, and operational support so creators can focus on producing content while Blue Wire handles ad sales and sponsorship coordination across a network of 200+ shows and 500+ creators reaching hundreds of millions of listeners. Backed by 500 Global. Blue Wire operates as a media and advertising business and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its company identity and domain-security posture within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Castbox
providers.description: Castbox is a free cross-platform podcast and audio content platform that lets listeners discover, stream, download, and manage millions of podcasts, audiobooks, and radio shows across Apple iOS, Android, Amazon Alexa, Google Home, CarPlay, Android Auto, and the web. Alongside its consumer listening apps, Castbox offers a "For Podcasters" suite for creators to host, distribute, and monetize their shows. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network, Castbox is a consumer audio company that publishes no public developer API portal; this profile captures its public identity, legal, and support surface.

providers.name: Crystal Dynamics
providers.description: Crystal Dynamics is a AAA video game development studio, best known as the home of the Tomb Raider franchise and its Lara Croft character, and part of the Embracer Group. The studio publishes a consumer-facing marketing website, careers portal, player support center, and news/community hub, but exposes no public developer API program, API documentation, developer portal, or SDKs. This profile entered the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio stub lead; enrichment confirms there is no public API surface to catalog at this time.

providers.name: Donut Media
providers.description: Donut Media is an American automotive entertainment brand and one of the largest automotive channels on YouTube, founded in 2015 by Matt Levin, Ben Conrad, and Nick Moceri. It is best known for original series such as Up to Speed, Money Pit, and HiLow, along with the Past Gas podcast, reaching millions of car enthusiasts through video, social, and audio. Donut monetizes through advertising, brand sponsorships, content licensing, and an extensive Shopify-powered online store selling apparel, hats, and collectibles. The company was acquired by Recurrent Ventures in November 2021. This profile documents Donut Media's public web and commerce surface; the company does not publish a developer API program.

providers.name: Jellysmack
providers.description: Jellysmack is a content amplification and creator-growth platform that helps digital creators expand their audiences and earnings across multiple social platforms (YouTube, Facebook, Snapchat, TikTok, Instagram) using AI-driven optimization, first-party data, and multi-platform distribution expertise. Its offerings span the Creator Program (audience growth and monetization for 500+ creator partners), Jellysmack Originals (owned beauty, sports, gaming, and entertainment channels), media licensing, and brand partnerships. The company reports 10B+ monthly video views and 125M+ monthly U.S. unique viewers. It is a consumer/creator-facing media technology company and does not publish a public developer API; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company/portfolio intelligence.

providers.name: Momox
providers.description: momox SE (formerly Momox AG / Momox GmbH) is a Berlin-based re-commerce company founded by Christian Wegner in 2004 — the name stands for "Moderner Medien Online Express-Ankauf" (Modern Media Online Express Purchase). Through momox.de it buys used books, CDs, DVDs/Blu-rays and games from private sellers at fixed prices in Germany, Austria, France, Belgium and the UK, reselling them via its Medimops shop and third-party marketplaces. Its momox fashion arm (formerly ubup.com, momoxfashion.com) does the same for second-hand clothing, shoes and accessories. momox runs large logistics centres in Berlin, Leipzig and Neuenhagen bei Berlin and has handled more than 350 million articles since founding. momox is a consumer-facing re-commerce operation; it publishes no official public developer program, API portal, or SDKs. The only machine surface is an internal, undocumented mobile-app pricing endpoint (api.momox.de / api.momox.fr) that is not offered as a first-party API.

providers.name: PortalOne
providers.description: PortalOne is a hybrid gaming platform that blends mobile games with live, interactive television-style entertainment, letting players compete inside shows and classic titles such as Atari's Breakout. Operated by PortalOne AS (Norway) and PortalOne, Inc. (United States), the company delivers its experience through native iOS and Android apps rather than a public developer platform. It is a consumer-facing entertainment product backed by Seedcamp and other venture investors; as of this profile PortalOne publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: Mars Reel
providers.description: Mars Reel (Mars Reel Media Corp) is a Los Angeles-based youth sports media and streaming company producing original basketball and soccer documentary series, athlete training content, and original episodic shows (The Vault, Like Mike, Game City). Its Mars Club membership provides premium on-demand video, and its TFIOM (The Future Is On Mars) label runs a Shopify fashion storefront. Mars Reel is a 500 Global portfolio company operating consumer web and streaming products. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or technical documentation; this profile captures its public identity and consumer link surface only.

providers.name: Onefootball
providers.description: Onefootball is a Berlin-based digital football (soccer) media platform that aggregates news, live scores, match coverage, video highlights, and streaming (OneFootball TV) for a global audience across iOS, Android, and the web. Backed by Earlybird and Union Square Ventures, the company partners with clubs, leagues, and publishers to distribute content and operates an official merchandise store and a Web3/club ecosystem. Onefootball does not publish a public developer API or partner developer portal; content ingestion for partners is handled via WordPress REST and private editorial integrations rather than an open, documented API surface.

providers.name: ProbablyMonsters
providers.description: ProbablyMonsters Inc. is an independent video game company headquartered in Bellevue, Washington, with a second location in Fort Worth, Texas. Founded in 2016 by former Bungie CEO Harold Ryan, it operates as a parent company that founds, funds and incubates development teams building AAA and AA interactive entertainment — publishing titles including Crimson Moon, Storm Lancers, IRE: A Prologue and Nekome. ProbablyMonsters sells finished games to players through console and PC storefronts; it is not a platform or developer-tools business. It publishes no developer program, no public API, no SDK and no machine-readable API description, and its GitHub organization carries zero public repositories. This profile records that absence with the probes behind it.

providers.name: Religion of Sports
providers.description: Religion of Sports is an Emmy Award-winning sports media and entertainment production studio founded in 2017 by Tom Brady, Michael Strahan and Gotham Chopra, headquartered in Santa Monica, California and operating as The Religion of Sports Media, Inc. The company produces premium non-fiction film, documentary series and branded content that examine why sports matter, distributed through Netflix, HBO, Paramount+, ESPN, Apple TV+, Showtime, Fox Sports and NBC Sports, with titles including Simone Biles Rising, In the Arena: Serena Williams, Made for March, 5-Star and Alex vs. ARod. It raised a $50M Series B led by Shamrock Capital in June 2022 to build a non-fiction studio arm and expand into new formats and non-sports categories. Its public surface is a marketing and press site; the company operates no developer program, publishes no API documentation, and exposes no machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Omnicom Group
providers.description: Omnicom Group Inc. (NYSE: OMC) is the world's largest marketing and sales communications holding company, formed in its current shape when Omnicom completed its acquisition of Interpublic Group on 26 November 2025, combining pro forma revenue in excess of $25 billion. The company operates across advertising, media, precision marketing, commerce, public relations, healthcare, branding, experiential and production, serving clients in more than 100 countries through agency networks including BBDO, DDB, TBWA, OMD, PHD, Hearts & Science, McCann, FCB, Mediabrands, Flywheel and Acxiom. Its Omni platform — built and operated by Annalect, Omnicom's data, technology and AI division — is marketed as an AI-driven marketing intelligence operating system spanning orchestration, production, predictive intelligence and outcome-driven activation, and is grounded in Acxiom Real ID identity data. As of the 2026-08-12 probe, Omnicom publishes no public developer program: no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL document, SDK, MCP server or A2A agent card is served from any Omnicom host. The corporate site moved from omnicomgroup.com to omc.com, which 301-redirects the legacy domain.

providers.name: Bustle
providers.description: Bustle is the flagship lifestyle and culture publication of Bustle Digital Group (BDG), a New York-based digital media company that moves culture forward through premium editorial content, social storytelling, and live experiences. BDG operates a portfolio of eight brands - Bustle, NYLON, Scary Mommy, W Magazine, Inverse, The Zoe Report, Romper, and Elite Daily - spanning lifestyle, fashion, parenting, entertainment, and luxury. The company produces award-winning branded content and campaigns through its BDG Studios and BDGx experiential arm. Bustle is a consumer media publisher rather than an API provider; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company/portfolio lead, and no public developer API or specification has been identified on its properties.

providers.name: Essence Ventures
providers.description: Essence Ventures is an independent, African American-owned media, technology, and commerce company focused on content, community, and commerce for Black women and their communities. Founded by Richelieu Dennis, it acquired Essence Communications (Essence magazine and the Essence Festival of Culture) in 2018, and its portfolio of lifestyle brands has included Afropunk, BeautyCon, and Essence Studios, reaching audiences across print, digital, video, social, and live events. Essence Ventures does not operate a public developer program or API; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company/portfolio lead awaiting further enrichment.

providers.name: Hooked
providers.description: Hooked is a mobile entertainment company founded in 2015 by Prerna Gupta and Parag Chordia (Telepathic, Inc.) that pioneered the chat-fiction format: bite-sized, suspenseful stories read as simulated text-message conversations. Its flagship Hooked app reached #1 on the App Store and Google Play in more than 25 countries and over 100 million viewers, and the company later launched Hooked TV, a short-form mobile video streaming service. Hooked uses data and AI to predict and produce hit short-form content distributed across its own apps and social platforms including TikTok, Instagram, Snapchat, and YouTube. It is backed by 500 Global, Cowboy Ventures, Sound Ventures, The Chernin Group, Founders Fund, and Greylock. Hooked does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDK.

providers.name: Overtime
providers.description: Overtime is a sports media and entertainment company building disruptive, digital-first sports leagues and intellectual property aimed at the next generation of fans and athletes. It operates branded leagues including Overtime Elite (OTE) basketball, OT7 seven-on-seven football, and OT Select women's basketball, and reaches nearly 100 million followers across social platforms. Backed by a16z, Overtime generates revenue through sponsorships, merchandise, media rights, and brand partnerships, reimagining how Gen Z engages with sports through content-first entertainment.

providers.name: Pilotly
providers.description: Pilotly is a media and content audience-testing research platform used by studios, streamers, and brands to test films, trailers, series, and advertising with targeted audiences before release. Its managed service pairs clients with expert research managers who handle survey design, audience targeting, and insights synthesis, while a Study Tracker guides each project through five stages (Requested, Setting up, Fielding, Analysis, Complete). Content is fielded through a secure, DRM-protected and watermarked video player across desktop, mobile, and smart TV. Pilotly is a managed-service SaaS with no public developer API surface; clients named on the site include Netflix, Amazon, Sony, Paramount, Warner Bros. Discovery, and Audible. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: TheSkimm
providers.description: TheSkimm is a digital media company founded in 2012 that curates news, lifestyle, money, career, and wellness content for a primarily female audience, delivered through email newsletters (the flagship Daily Skimm, plus Well Played, Skimm Well + Good, and Skimm Shopping), a mobile app, podcasts, and shopping guides. It is now part of Everyday Health, Inc., a Ziff Davis company. TheSkimm operates as a consumer media and audience business rather than an API provider: it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications. This API Evangelist profile was seeded as a portfolio lead of GV (Google Ventures) and enriched with the company's public identity, link properties, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Vioo
providers.description: Vioo is a Mexican professional visual-content platform that connects businesses with a national network of 1,500+ certified photographers and creators across Mexico, delivering photography, videography, drone footage, 3D renders, and Matterport virtual tours. It serves real estate, gastronomy, e-commerce, hospitality, events, and portrait use cases with AI-assisted editing and 48-hour delivery, and offers scheduling either through a personalized form or automatically via an integration API. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Beme
providers.description: Beme Inc. (stylized "beme") was an American multimedia company founded in 2014 in New York City by YouTube filmmaker Casey Neistat and engineer Matt Hackett. Its mobile app, released on iOS in July 2015 and on Android in May 2016, let users capture and instantly share unedited two-to-eight-second videos without previewing or editing them, aiming at a more authentic alternative to curated social video. Beme raised a seed round backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Vayner/RSE, and CNN acquired the company in November 2016 in a deal reported at $25 million. The consumer app was shut down on January 31, 2017, and on January 25, 2018 the founders departed and Beme was folded into CNN Digital Studios. The company is defunct. Beme never published a public API, developer portal, or API documentation; its only public technical artifact is an open-source Go testing utility. The beme.com domain has since changed hands and now redirects to an unrelated company.

providers.name: Beatport
providers.description: Beatport is the leading online music store and streaming platform for electronic dance music DJs and producers, founded in 2004 and headquartered in Denver, Colorado. Beatport sells high-quality downloads (lossless WAV, AIFF, and FLAC, plus AAC) of tracks, releases, and DJ tools across more than 150 electronic genres, and operates a subscription streaming tier — Beatport Streaming — that delivers catalog tracks directly into supported DJ applications and hardware including Pioneer DJ rekordbox, Serato DJ Pro, Denon DJ Engine DJ, Algoriddim djay, Virtual DJ, Traktor, and others through integration partners. The Beatport Group also operates Beatsource (open- format DJ streaming and download store), DJCity (open-format record pool), Beatport LINK and Beatsource LINK (in-app streaming for DJ software), BeatportAmp (distribution and rights management for labels, formerly Ampsuite), Plugin Boutique (audio software and plugin marketplace), Loopcloud (sample subscription for producers), Label Radar (demo submission), Beatport Live (live events and streaming), Beatportal (editorial and media), and the International Music Summit (IMS) industry conference. The company reports ten million registered users, eighty thousand labels, four hundred thousand artists, and four hundred million USD paid out to rights holders since launch. Beatport operates a v4 REST API at api.beatport.com governed by OAuth 2.0 (authorization-code grant) with an interactive Swagger-UI developer portal at /v4/docs/; access is gated to approved partners through the Beatport Partner Portal, and there is no public client-credentials tier for general developers. The API exposes the Beatport catalog (tracks, releases, artists, labels, genres, sub-genres, charts, playlists, my-beatport collections, holds, and DJ-oriented search filters such as BPM, key, and released-date) and is the same surface that powers the public beatport.com applications and third-party DJ-software integrations. Beatport does not publish a downloadable OpenAPI document, an official SDK, or a CLI; partner integration is brokered case-by-case through the Partner Portal and the business-development team.

providers.name: OUTFRONT Media
providers.description: OUTFRONT Media is a U.S. out-of-home (OOH) advertising company and real estate investment trust (NYSE: OUT) operating a national portfolio of billboards, digital displays, and transit advertising assets. The company runs the MTA Advertising Network across New York City's subways, buses, and commuter rail, along with roadside billboards, digital liveboards, Times Square spectaculars, and place-based displays in major U.S. markets. OUTFRONT's digital inventory is made available programmatically through DOOH supply-side partners such as Vistar Media and Place Exchange. OUTFRONT sold its Canadian operations to Bell Media in October 2022 to focus on the U.S. market. OUTFRONT does not publish a developer portal or public APIs; programmatic access to its inventory is mediated through third-party DOOH SSPs.

providers.name: SureWaves
providers.description: SureWaves is a broadcast-television advertising technology company that integrates linear TV with digital advertising infrastructure. It provides AI-powered spot and yield management for broadcasters and real-time, pay-for-performance campaign tooling for advertisers, and operates India's largest spot TV network — more than 20 million spots monthly across 550+ local channels reaching 490+ million households. Holder of 50+ patents, backed by Accel, with offices in Bangalore, New York, McLean, Mumbai and New Delhi. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; two enrichment passes (2026-07 and 2026-08) found no public API, developer portal, SDK, package, or machine-readable contract of any kind — the platform is sold as an enterprise engagement behind a "Request Meeting" form. The company does display a SOC 2 Type II badge on its homepage, attested by Prescient Assurance against AICPA SSAE 18.

providers.name: Weshine
providers.description: Weshine (闪萌, Shanmeng), operated by Beijing Shanqu Information Technology Co., Ltd (北京闪趣信息技术有限公司), is a Chinese GIF and animated-sticker (表情) search engine. It offers a business-to-business "Expression API" (表情API) with three documented interfaces — a hot/trending interface (热门接口) that returns trending GIFs by category refreshed hourly, a real-time search interface (搜索接口) supporting gif/webp/mp4 and multi-dimensional ranking, and a "magic image" interface (神配图接口) that semantically matches a phrase to a background GIF and composites a caption onto it. The platform reports 800M+ users covered, 300M+ daily searches, and 200M+ animated images sent per day, powering social apps, input methods (including its own KK Keyboard), and browsers. API access is via business partnership; no public self-serve developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDK is published.

providers.name: bith.tv
providers.description: Bith.ai (bith.tv) is an all-in-one, AI-powered video editing and content creation platform for creators, letting users record, edit, resize, caption, and publish short-form video reformatted for the major social platforms from a single browser-based dashboard. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Amman, Jordan, the company is backed by 500 Global, BeyondCapital, Propeller, and Oasis500. Bith does not currently expose a public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio lead and enriched with what the company publicly publishes (website, marketing tool pages, pricing, sign-up, and probed domain security posture).

providers.name: Cheddar
providers.description: Cheddar is a business and technology news media company producing live and on-demand video, articles, and newsletters covering financial markets, technology, innovation, entrepreneurship, and culture for a modern digital audience. Founded as a millennial-focused financial news network and backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Ribbit Capital, Comcast Ventures, and Altice USA, Cheddar streams programming such as Opening Bell, Big Business This Week, and NYSE TV Live across its website, connected-TV apps, and social platforms. It operates as a digital media and content publisher rather than an API or developer-platform company; this profile tracks Cheddar within the API Evangelist network and carries no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: DayDayCook
providers.description: DayDayCook is a home-cooking content-to-commerce platform founded in Hong Kong that publishes recipes, cooking videos, and food storytelling (its "Taste & Tales" blog) alongside a direct-to-consumer shop selling its own branded sauces, ingredients, and prepared foods under the tagline "Easy Cooking, Festive Flavours." The business pairs a culinary media audience with a consumer-packaged-goods and e-commerce operation. It is a portfolio company of 500 Global and is tracked in the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass DayDayCook publishes a consumer web presence and online shop but exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Kaiber
providers.description: Kaiber (Kyber Corp., dba Kaiber) is an AI creative studio for generative video and audio. Its web and mobile apps let creators turn text prompts, images, and music into stylized videos through features such as Canvas, Beat Sync, Auto-Clip, and an Editor timeline, sold via credit-based monthly subscription plans (Starter, Creator, Pro, Visionary) plus day passes and one-time credit packs. Kaiber does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile tracks the company's identity and public web properties in the API Evangelist network, surfaced originally as a portfolio company of eqt-ventures.

providers.name: Shibuya
providers.description: Shibuya is a platform for curated short films and the independent creators behind them, describing itself as a home where fans help greenlight the future of film and audiences discover original storytelling. Operated by NotShibuya, Inc. and backed by a16z, Shibuya began as a web3 storytelling experiment and has grown into a community-driven curation platform for short-form film, winning a 2025 Primetime Emmy for Outstanding Innovation in Emerging Media Programming. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Shibuya publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its real public web properties.

providers.name: Bleacher Report
providers.description: Bleacher Report is a digital sports media company headquartered in San Francisco and owned by Warner Bros. Discovery (Turner Sports). Founded in 2007, it delivers sports news, live scores, highlights, video, and community-driven commentary across the web and its iOS and Android applications, spanning the NFL, NBA, MLB, soccer, and other leagues. Bleacher Report maintains a public GitHub organization with open source engineering projects but does not publish a public developer API program; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Uncork Capital and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Fox Corporation
providers.description: Fox Corporation (NASDAQ: FOXA, FOX) is a US media company spun out of 21st Century Fox in 2019 when the rest of the business was sold to Disney. Per the company website, "Fox Corporation produces and distributes compelling news, sports, and entertainment content through its primary iconic domestic brands" — Fox News Media (Fox News Channel, Fox Business Network, Fox News Digital, Fox News Audio, Fox Weather), Fox Sports (FS1, FS2, Big Ten Network, Fox Deportes, Fox Bet partnerships), Fox Entertainment, Fox Television Stations, and the Tubi Media Group (Tubi free ad-supported streaming, Credible). In May 2024 Fox acquired Mexican sports-betting and casino operator Caliente.mx, expanding its sports-and-wagering footprint into Latin America. Fox does not publish a public developer portal or REST API surface for the parent corporation — programmatic distribution is delivered via per-brand RSS / Atom feeds (Fox News, Fox Business, Fox Sports, Fox Weather), the Tubi Media Group open source projects on GitHub (github.com/Tubitv, 53 public repositories), and direct B2B advertising and content-syndication relationships rather than self-serve API signup. This apis.yml therefore catalogs the public RSS surface, Tubi engineering OSS, and the corporate/brand web properties.

providers.name: Supponor
providers.description: Supponor is a virtual advertising technology company for live sports broadcasting, now part of TGI Sport. Its software digitally replaces and inserts in-venue brand placements with real-time overlays, letting broadcasters serve region-targeted advertising across multiple feeds, languages, surfaces, and camera angles. Core products include AIR, an AI-driven virtual advertising platform for live broadcast; HUB, a pre-event suite for fixtures, inventory, playlists, creative and approvals; and Data Room, a post-event analytics platform for reporting, video storage, and performance metrics. Supponor works across any sport and surface with remotely deployable, all-weather technology, and is used by organizations including FC Bayern, the NHL, The FA, Serie A, and La Liga. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Northzone; it publishes a corporate and careers web presence but no public developer API surface.

providers.name: RealNetworks
providers.description: RealNetworks is a Seattle-based technology company that pairs AI-powered computer-vision and secure-communication products with its long-running consumer media brands. Its portfolio includes SAFR (facial recognition for security and retail loss prevention), Kontxt (AI messaging and voice security for CPaaS platforms, Telcos, and MNOs), GameHouse (cross-device casual gaming), and RealPlayer (media playback). Product APIs for SAFR and Kontxt are delivered through authenticated partner portals rather than an open developer portal; the historical Real Developer Program (developer.real.com) is no longer live, and no public OpenAPI specification was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Audacy
providers.description: Audacy, Inc. is a U.S. multi-platform audio and entertainment company that operates the country's second-largest radio group alongside the Audacy streaming app, a major podcast network, and the Amperwave audio ad-tech and distribution platform. Formerly known as Entercom (rebranded to Audacy on March 30, 2021), the company filed prepackaged Chapter 11 bankruptcy on January 7, 2024 and emerged on September 30, 2024 as a privately held company after equitizing approximately $1.6 billion of funded debt and reducing total debt from roughly $1.9 billion to $350 million. The current portfolio spans ~230 radio brands across 47 markets, 200+ million monthly listeners, ~2 billion annual podcast downloads, and the Cadence13, Pineapple Street Studios, Podcorn, and BetMGM Network (formerly BetQL) audio brands. There is no public developer API, no published OpenAPI, and no GitHub organization with public repositories; integration is brokered through ad sales, programmatic marketplaces, and the Amperwave platform.

providers.name: HAAWK
providers.description: HAAWK is a Los Angeles-based music rights management and monetization company that administers digital rights across YouTube, Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok for record labels, music publishers, and independent artists. Its products include HAAWK (full-service YouTube Content ID and Meta Rights Manager administration), Identifyy (self-service UGC rights management for independent creators), Keyframe Audio (a micro sync-licensing catalog of 50,000+ production music tracks), and Diistro (digital music distribution to Apple Music, Spotify, YouTube Music, and TikTok). HAAWK has administered 100B+ video views and manages 1.1M+ music copyrights for 2,000+ rights holders. Backed by 500 Global. No public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: MightyHive
providers.description: MightyHive was a data and digital media consultancy that helped brands take control of their programmatic advertising, media buying, data strategy, and marketing technology. Founded as an independent programmatic trading and media consultancy, it was acquired by S4 Capital and rebranded to Media.Monks in August 2021; the S4 Capital operating company has since consolidated under the single "Monks" brand (monks.com). Its offerings spanned digital media transformation, campaign launch and measurement, customer data platform (CDP) work, Amazon eCommerce solutions, and marketing/AI transformation services for enterprise brands. It is a professional-services / consulting business, not an API product company: it publishes no public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, machine-readable specification, or client SDK on any package registry. It does keep a public GitHub organization (github.com/MightyHive, named "Media.Monks (formerly MightyHive)") of internal tooling, Looker blocks and ML notebooks, but nothing there is a released API or client library. The legacy mightyhive.com domain still resolves and serves a frozen archive of pre-2021 press and case studies. Added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z-portfolio lead; repeated enrichment confirms no API surface exists.

providers.name: Baller League
providers.description: Baller League is a small-sided (six-a-side) football entertainment league and media format founded in Germany that bills itself as "a new era of football, created for the streets by the streets." Teams are captained by professional footballers, influencers, and streamers, with matches played under a fast-paced ruleset and distributed primarily through live streaming and social video (Twitch, YouTube, TikTok, Instagram) rather than traditional broadcast. The organization has expanded from Germany into the United Kingdom and United States and is running its fourth season. It is a consumer sports-media and entertainment brand; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, documentation, or developer program. Backed by EQT Ventures and tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company.

providers.name: Blavity
providers.description: Blavity Inc. is a Black-owned digital media and technology company founded in 2014 by Morgan DeBaun, operating a portfolio of premium content brands and events for Black millennials and Gen Z around culture, technology, travel, and lifestyle. Its properties include Blavity.com (news and culture), AfroTech (the largest Black tech conference and media brand), Travel Noire (travel), Shadow and Act (film and entertainment), and 21Ninety (women's lifestyle). Blavity Inc. monetizes through advertising, branded content, events, and its Blavity Media Group agency. It is a privately held company backed by investors including 500 Global and GV, and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specifications. This profile tracks Blavity as a company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Business Insider
providers.description: Business Insider is a global business and financial news media company founded in 2007 and headquartered in New York City, operating as part of Axel Springer. It publishes fast-paced coverage of markets, technology, finance, the economy, retail, media, and careers across its flagship Business Insider brand and verticals such as Markets Insider. The organization was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of the venture firm IVP. It operates consumer news properties and content syndication feeds rather than a public developer API program, so this profile tracks its public web presence and domain security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Clicker
providers.description: Clicker is a consumer-facing streaming guide and discovery platform that helps people find where to watch popular and new movies and TV shows across streaming providers, aggregating title availability from services such as Netflix, Hulu, Disney+, Max, Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV+, Paramount+, Peacock, Starz, BET+, Philo, and FuboTV into a single searchable catalog. The product is a web application (Next.js) organized around TV Shows and Movies browse and search experiences. Clicker is backed by Redpoint Ventures. As of this enrichment pass Clicker publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or developer documentation; its only backend surface is a private, robots disallowed internal application API.

providers.name: Mad Realities
providers.description: Mad Realities is a creator-powered entertainment network that produces original episodic shows for internet-native audiences, bridging the gap between culture born online and television-level production by partnering with creators. Its Mad Labs arm is an R&D effort leveraging AI and technology to superpower creatives. Backed by Paradigm, the company operates as a consumer media brand and publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform at this time.

providers.name: Powder
providers.description: Powder was a Paris-based gaming company, founded in 2018 and backed by a $14M Series A led by Serena with General Catalyst, Slow Ventures, Alven, Bpifrance Digital Venture and Secocha Ventures. It built AI-powered clipping software for gamers and content creators: a low-resource Windows screen recorder plus on-device machine learning that detected highlight moments in gameplay recordings and long Twitch, YouTube and Kick streams and turned them into short vertical clips, AutoEdits and automontages, with per-title models for 40-plus games including Fortnite, Valorant, Counter-Strike 2 and League of Legends, and NPU-accelerated local inference on AMD XDNA hardware. It was distributed as an end-user desktop app through Steam, the Microsoft Store and Razer Cortex, on a free tier with a $9.99/month Powder Pro subscription. Powder published no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract. The company has since wound down: its own apex domain now redirects every path to a first-party notice stating the app is no longer updated or maintained and that all subscriptions have been cancelled.

providers.name: Rigi
providers.description: Rigi (Rigi TV) is an instant-entertainment mobile app that streams quick, captivating, and scroll-worthy short-form video and micro-drama series across genres such as romance, drama, thriller, and suspense. Operated out of HSR Layout in Bengaluru, Karnataka, India and backed by Accel, it delivers on-demand vertical entertainment through its Android app. It is a consumer-facing streaming product; no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal surface is currently published.

providers.name: Syncbak
providers.description: Syncbak is a Marion, Iowa media-technology company founded in 2009 by Jack Perry that built the streaming infrastructure local U.S. television broadcasters use to put their over-the-air signals online. Its SimpleSync / MediaMogul platform handles live-stream transcoding, cloud-based rights resolution and geo-location authentication, cloud DVR, device filtering, content management, stream monitoring, clipping, and dynamic ad insertion through its AdSync product, delivering station feeds to OTT destinations including Paramount+, Hulu, fuboTV, Amazon, Roku, Apple TV and the NFL across 200+ U.S. markets. The company rebranded to Zeam Media in May 2024 to match its Zeam consumer hyperlocal streaming app, and syncbak.com now redirects to zeammedia.com. Syncbak publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable contract; its platform is delivered to broadcasters and station groups under commercial agreement.

providers.name: turntable
providers.description: turntable (Turntable Labs) is a consumer social-music company originally surfaced as a portfolio company of slow-ventures and union-square-ventures. The original Turntable.fm social listening service shut down in 2013 and its domain no longer resolves. The lineage lives on at Turntable Labs, which operates two consumer music products - Hangout (a social music-streaming and group-chat app at hangout.fm / hang.fm) and Turntable (a create-share-and-vibe GenAI music experience). No public API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation are published for any of these products - this is a consumer application, not an API provider. Enrichment probes (DNS, HTTP, site fetch) confirmed no developer surface as of 2026-07-21.

providers.name: Time Warner
providers.description: Time Warner was a Fortune 500 American multinational mass media and entertainment conglomerate, one of the largest media companies in the world until its acquisition by AT&T in 2018. It operated major brands including HBO, CNN, Turner Broadcasting, Warner Bros., and DC Comics. After the AT&T acquisition it was rebranded as WarnerMedia. In 2022, WarnerMedia merged with Discovery Inc. to form Warner Bros. Discovery. Time Warner did not offer a public developer API platform.

providers.name: Red Ventures
providers.description: Red Ventures is a privately held digital marketing and media holding company headquartered in Fort Mill, South Carolina, operating a portfolio of high-growth consumer comparison, commerce, education, and content businesses including Bankrate, The Points Guy, Lonely Planet, Allconnect, Sage Home Loans, RV Education, and RV Home Client Services. The company combines proprietary technology, data science, and performance marketing to acquire customers on behalf of its brands and partners. It maintains a public GitHub organization of 77 largely-forked internal engineering repositories and a company blog, but publishes no public developer API program: there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL contract, first-party SDK, or served /.well-known/ discovery document on any Red Ventures-controlled host.

providers.name: CohnReznick
providers.description: CohnReznick is a top-25 US accounting, tax, and advisory firm formed in 2012 by the merger of J.H. Cohn LLP and Reznick Group, P.C. The firm serves clients across more than 30 industries from offices throughout the United States and four offshore subsidiaries, with its global reach extended through membership in the Nexia International network (operating in more than 128 countries). In May 2024 CohnReznick became the first US accounting firm of its scale to receive a strategic growth investment from a private equity sponsor when funds advised by Apax Partners acquired a majority stake. As part of that transaction the firm operates under an alternative-practice structure: audit and attest services are delivered by CohnReznick LLP (a licensed CPA firm) while tax and advisory services are delivered through CohnReznick Advisory LLC. Largest practice areas include Real Estate, Renewable Energy, Government Contracting, Asset Management (private equity, hedge funds, private credit, REITs), Financial Services, Healthcare, Life Sciences, Consumer & Industrial, Technology & Media, Public Sector, and Private Clients (family offices, high net worth individuals, professional sports). CohnReznick does not publish a public software developer API; this repository documents the firm's organizational profile, practice taxonomy, and linked-data context for API catalog purposes.

providers.name: Every.tv
providers.description: Every, Inc. (株式会社エブリー, corp.every.tv) is a Tokyo-based Japanese video-media and advertising company that runs consumer lifestyle products including DELISH KITCHEN (recipe video media), retailHUB (a retail promotion and data platform connecting physical stores with digital channels), トモニテ / Tomonite (parenting video media and community), and MOMENTH (a professional video production and social team). Led by CEO Taissei Yoshida and headquartered in Roppongi, Minato, Tokyo, the company approached an IPO on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Growth Market. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Every, Inc. publishes an engineering blog and owned media but exposes no public developer API program.

providers.name: ilovewoof
providers.description: ilovewoof (ilovewoof.com) is a UK-focused pet-care and lifestyle content publication covering companion animals and wildlife. It publishes pet-care guides, behavioral insights, health articles, rescue stories, and animal-world news across four sections — Cats, Dogs, News, and Other pets (small and exotic animals) — with health and medical content reviewed by licensed veterinary professionals, and offers a weekly email newsletter. It is an editorial content site, not an API provider; no public API, developer documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable interface was found during enrichment. Surfaced as a qiming portfolio lead and profiled in the API Evangelist network for completeness.

providers.name: TMRW Sports
providers.description: TMRW Sports is a sports, media, and entertainment company founded by professional golfers Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy, with Mike McCarley as Founder and CEO, focused on building modern, tech-forward approaches to live sports. Its ventures include TGL, a primetime team golf league played in partnership with the PGA TOUR; WTGL, a professional women's golf league; and a professional flag football league launching in partnership with the NFL. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bessemer-venture-partners, TMRW Sports operates consumer sports and entertainment properties and does not publish a public developer platform, API, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Craon
providers.description: Craon (craon.ai) is an AI-native video editing platform where users edit through natural-language chat instead of a traditional timeline. Creators describe their intent in plain language — "make this more cinematic", "build tension before the reveal", "warm golden-hour grade" — and Craon's AI performs the cuts, color grading, pacing, silence removal, scene detection, subtitle generation, and emotional storytelling automatically. It targets content creators, YouTubers, social and short-form creators, filmmakers, and marketing teams who want professional results without timeline experience or color-theory skills, positioning itself as an AI-native alternative to CapCut, Adobe Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, iMovie, Filmora, Runway, and Descript. Craon is an early-stage company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. The product is a consumer web application with no public developer API; its only machine-facing surface today is a published /llms.txt for AI discovery.

providers.name: Art19
providers.description: Art19 (ART19, Inc.) is a podcast hosting, distribution, and monetization platform, and an Amazon company. It provides publishers, networks, and enterprises with a content management system for audio, automated RSS feed generation, dynamic ad insertion and targeting through its WarpFeed feed technology, and an embeddable Web Player. The platform serves podcast delivery, analytics, and advertising workflows at scale. Art19 does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal; its public presence consists of a marketing site, a contact page, a privacy policy, and a system status page tracking CMS, RSS, WarpFeed, and Web Player availability.

providers.name: BallerTV
providers.description: BallerTV (Baller, Inc.) is a Pasadena, California sports media company that live streams and provides on-demand replays and highlights of youth and amateur sports, including basketball, volleyball, soccer, lacrosse, softball, and football, from thousands of tournaments and showcases nationwide. Subscribers range from families following athletes to NCAA and professional scouts using the footage for recruiting and scouting. The platform includes a Game Finder for locating events, purchasable athlete highlight reels, and BTVision, an AI-powered ball-tracking streaming technology that improves the basketball viewing experience. BallerTV is a consumer streaming product delivered through its website and iOS/Android apps; it does not publish a public developer API or SDK program. This profile was surfaced as an index-ventures portfolio company and enriched from public web sources.

providers.name: DAZN
providers.description: DAZN is a global over-the-top live sports streaming service headquartered in London and owned by Access Industries. Launched in 2015 out of the former Perform Group, it streams boxing, football, MotoGP, UFC and other rights to subscribers across more than 200 countries and territories, and has expanded through the acquisitions of Eleven Group, Foxtel/Kayo Sports and ViewLift, alongside the DAZN Bet and DAZN Media brands. DAZN operates a large Node.js microservice estate on AWS and publishes open source engineering tooling (the Kopytko Roku ecosystem, dazn-lambda-powertools) from its GitHub organization, but it runs no public developer program: there is no developer portal, no API reference, and no machine-readable specification for the consumer platform APIs that power its apps.

providers.name: Huckberry
providers.description: Huckberry is an American direct-to-consumer online retailer of men's apparel, outdoor gear and lifestyle goods, founded in 2010 by Andy Forch and Richard Greiner and headquartered in San Francisco with offices in Austin and Columbus. It pairs a first-party e-commerce storefront with a large editorial operation — the Huckberry Journal — and an in-house brand portfolio, selling an "everyday adventure" assortment that sits between traditional outdoor retail and menswear. Huckberry is a retailer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer program, no public API, no SDK and no machine-readable contract. Its public GitHub organization (Huckberry Inc) holds eight repositories, seven of them forks of third-party Ruby e-commerce gems — Solidus AvaTax, Affirm, Paperclip, omniauth-slack — which evidence a self-hosted Ruby storefront rather than a published platform. Partner and affiliate integration is outsourced to the Partnerize network, and customer self-service runs on a Zendesk help center tenant at help.huckberry.com.

providers.name: EIN Newswire
providers.description: Paid and free press release distribution services are in one place. The EIN Presswire offers the best press release service that helps you to reach your target market with minimal effort.

providers.name: Drone Racing League
providers.description: The Drone Racing League (DRL) is a New York-based professional drone racing property founded in 2015 by Nicholas Horbaczewski, staging first-person-view (FPV) races in which pilots fly identical, league-built quadcopters - the Racer series - through three-dimensional courses in stadiums, arenas and landmark venues at speeds above 80 mph. DRL designs its own racing drones, timing and telemetry hardware, produces and distributes its race broadcasts across NBC, Sky Sports, ProSiebenSat.1 and streaming platforms, and operates the DRL Simulator, an FPV racing game on Steam, PlayStation and Xbox that feeds the Swatch DRL Tryouts esports pipeline used to recruit professional pilots. The company was acquired by Infinite Reality (now Napster) in April 2024. DRL publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API specification, and as of the 2026-08-04 enrichment pass its primary web properties (thedroneracingleague.com, drl.io) were not completing a TLS handshake.

providers.name: Mediaspectrum
providers.description: Mediaspectrum is a cloud-based SaaS provider of multichannel advertising, content management, and publishing software for media companies and publishers. Founded in 2001 and headquartered in Miami, its platform manages the full advertising lifecycle -- proposal generation, packaging, scheduling, rating, workflow, trafficking, optimization, and billing -- alongside an integrated CRM and the ContentWatch content management system spanning print, web, mobile, video, social, and broadcast channels. The company raised a $35.8M investment from Insight Venture Partners in 2013 and counts Gannett, Dow Jones, and Trinity Mirror among its clients. No public API, developer portal, or SDKs are published as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Vedantu
providers.description: Vedantu is an Indian online-learning (edtech) company headquartered in Bangalore that delivers LIVE interactive classes, recorded courses, offline centres, and one-to-one tutoring for school students from Class 1 to 12 and competitive-exam aspirants, covering CBSE, ICSE, IGCSE and major State Boards plus JEE, NEET, CUET and Olympiad preparation, alongside a large free library of NCERT solutions, revision notes, sample papers and study material. Backed by Accel, Vedantu is consumer-facing and operates no public developer API today; its only published integration surface is a legacy External-Integration (EI) kit for institutes on GitHub, though it does publish an llms.txt for agents.

providers.name: Photobucket
providers.description: Photobucket is a consumer image and video hosting service founded in 2003 and now operated by Photobucket Inc. of Seattle. It provides cloud photo/video storage, organization, and private group sharing through subscription plans (My Bucket and +Group Buckets, each including 1TB of storage) alongside a free tier. Historically one of the largest image-hosting platforms on the early social web, Photobucket opened a public developer API in 2008, but no current public/documented API surface could be found during enrichment: the developer portal is bot-blocked, the GitHub organization holds only forks and hiring challenges (no official SDK), and the app runs as a single-page application with no published /.well-known/ discovery documents. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Trinity Ventures.

providers.name: TripScout
providers.description: TripScout is a travel media and deals company that curates flight and hotel recommendations for consumers and operates a portfolio of large travel-focused social brands (including the @hotel property at athotel.com). Its core product scans millions of flights weekly and emails subscribers a small set of vetted deals, each paired with featured, splurge, and budget hotel options plus destination context such as weather, festivals, and local activities. TripScout runs a free tier (one deal per week) and a premium subscription. It is a consumer-facing, email- and social-first business and does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation portal, or SDKs. Backed by 500 Global; added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead.

providers.name: Rebel Girls
providers.description: Rebel Girls is a global media and publishing brand that celebrates inspiring stories about girls and women, empowering young audiences through books, a podcast, a YouTube channel, apparel and accessories, activities, and the Rebel Girls Sport program. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass Rebel Girls publishes no developer, API, or well-known discovery surface: rebelgirls.com redirects to www.rebelgirls.com and every standard well-known endpoint returns 404, and there are no developer/api subdomains. This profile captures the company's public identity and a live domain-security posture probe; it carries no API artifacts because there is no public API to describe.

providers.name: BLAST
providers.description: BLAST is a Danish esports and gaming entertainment company headquartered in Copenhagen, founded in 2016. It produces and operates premier competitive gaming tournaments and leagues (notably Counter-Strike BLAST Premier) and runs the blast.tv streaming and fan-engagement platform, delivering live events, broadcasts, and interactive esports content to a global audience. Backed by Creandum, Heartcore, Maki.vc, and Vaekstfonden, BLAST was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead company. No public developer API, portal, or documentation surface was found during enrichment; this profile captures verifiable identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Digg
