providers.description: Digg is a technology news aggregation and community curation platform, relaunched under new ownership and backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and True Ventures. It surfaces trending stories, discussions, and video signals drawn largely from X/Twitter, ranking them by community engagement and editorial signals. The platform tracks contributor rankings, rising stories, today's highlights, and GitHub repository activity, positioning itself as an AI-assisted discovery hub for technology, startups, and AI news. As surfaced here, Digg is a consumer web product with no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation; this profile captures its identity and web/domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Lunar-X
providers.description: Lunar-X (Lunar X) is a global digital content studio that acquires, develops, and operates creator-driven entertainment brands into globally recognized franchises across animation, educational content, functional music, ecommerce, and live events. Its properties include Economics Explained, Theorist Inc, Music Labs, and Lunar Kids, collectively spanning tens of billions of views and over a hundred million subscribers. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Creandum and added to the API Evangelist network. As a media/content operator it publishes a marketing website and privacy policy but exposes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Take Two
providers.description: Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. (NASDAQ: TTWO) is a leading developer, publisher, and marketer of interactive entertainment for consumers worldwide, headquartered in New York City. The company delivers its products principally through three wholly owned labels — Rockstar Games, 2K, and Zynga — spanning console, PC, and mobile platforms via physical retail, digital download, online platforms, and cloud streaming. Franchises include Grand Theft Auto, Red Dead Redemption, NBA 2K, Borderlands, and mobile titles such as Words With Friends and Toon Blast. Take-Two is a publicly traded interactive entertainment holding company; it does not publish a public developer API program, developer portal, or API documentation at the corporate level. This profile was surfaced as a general-catalyst job-board listing and carried into the API Evangelist network as a lead; enrichment found no public API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Viacom
providers.description: Viacom was an American mass media conglomerate that merged with CBS Corporation in December 2019 to form ViacomCBS (later rebranded as Paramount Global). The combined entity, which included brands such as CBS, MTV, Nickelodeon, Comedy Central, BET, Paramount Pictures, Showtime, and Paramount+, was subsequently acquired by Skydance Media and ceased to exist as an independent public company in August 2025. Viacom maintained open source software through its GitHub organization (ViacomInc), including tools for Roku channel development, tvOS UI components, and broadcast calendar utilities. No public external developer API program was offered.

providers.name: Glimmer (formerly Storyhunter)
providers.description: Glimmer, formerly known as Storyhunter, is an all-in-one creator management platform and global marketplace connecting brands and media companies with a vetted network of 50,000+ freelance content creators, video producers, and journalists across 170+ countries. Founded in 2012 by Jaron Gilinsky in Brooklyn, New York, and rebranded from Storyhunter to Glimmer in November 2023, the platform organizes creator teams, messaging, project management, online contracts, and global payments in one central dashboard, and offers Glimmer Select as a full-service managed production studio. Clients have included CNN, The New York Times, National Geographic, MSNBC, and Starbucks. The company was backed in part by 500 Global and is surfaced here as an API Evangelist network company profile; it does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Edgeware
providers.description: Edgeware AB was a Swedish video-delivery technology company founded in 2004 and headquartered in Stockholm, known for its TV CDN, origin and media server, and streaming video-delivery products used by telecom operators and broadcasters to run OTT and IPTV services. Backed by Creandum, it listed on Nasdaq Stockholm in 2016 and was acquired by Agile Content (Agile Content S.A.) in 2020. The Edgeware brand has since been consolidated into AgileTV: edgeware.tv now redirects to agiletv.com/edgeware/, and its developer/technical documentation lives under docs.agilecontent.com (AgileTV Origin & Media Server, CDN Solutions, Subtitling). Edgeware no longer operates as an independent company or publishes an independent developer API surface.

providers.name: Spext Labs, Spext
providers.description: Spext (Spext Labs) is an AI-powered audio and video editing platform that lets users edit recordings by trimming an auto-generated transcript rather than a waveform — a text-first "recording management system" for podcasts, interviews and other spoken-word media. Backed by 500 Global, the company operates from a Framer-hosted marketing site (spext.co) and a web application (app.spext.co). As of this enrichment pass Spext exposes no public developer surface — no documented API, developer portal, SDKs, OpenAPI, or well-known discovery endpoints were found; the profile is retained as a network company record.

providers.name: Airborne Entertainment
providers.description: Airborne Entertainment was a Montreal, Quebec mobile entertainment company founded in 2000 that published and distributed premium mobile content and applications for carrier decks and early smartphones, including games, ringtones, ring-back tones, images, video and informational content, often under licensed consumer brands. The company raised a $22M round in July 2004 with participation from Insight Partners and Verizon, sold a majority stake to Japan's CYBIRD Co., Ltd. in 2005, was taken back by management in a 2008 buy-out, operated afterwards as Airborne Mobile, and was acquired by Bandsintown in October 2010. It no longer operates as an independent company: both airborneentertainment.com and airbornemobile.com are parked domain-sale listings, and the company never published a public developer portal, API, or SDK surface. This profile is retained as an API Evangelist network history record.

providers.name: fuboTV
providers.description: Fubo (fuboTV) is a live TV streaming service focused on sports, offering more than 100 live channels covering the NFL, NBA, MLB, soccer, Formula 1, NASCAR and major broadcast networks (ABC, NBC, CBS, FOX), alongside news, entertainment and on-demand content. The service includes cloud DVR, multi-device streaming and no-commitment monthly plans. fuboTV was surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures and northzone and added to the API Evangelist network. It is a direct-to-consumer streaming brand and does not publish a public developer API program; this profile captures its public web, legal, security and identity surface.

providers.name: Market Vibe
providers.description: MarketVibe (marketvibe.com) is a finance and technology news blog that publishes ongoing coverage under the tagline "The Financial Status of the World" — market trends, startup funding, and developer-focused technology news (for example, recurring roundups of Replit funding talks, feature releases, and AI developments). It is a WordPress.com / Newspack-hosted publication organized into Tech, Finance, and Lifestyle categories, offering articles and an RSS feed rather than a developer API product. It was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment found a content/media site with no product API surface (only the default WordPress REST API at /wp-json/).

providers.name: KAMI
providers.description: KAMI (Çizgi Studio) is a next-generation transmedia entertainment platform out of Turkey that lets a community read, write, and live inside stories. The mobile app and web platform offer thousands of original webtoons, comics (çizgi roman), novels, and AI-character chat across genres like romance, thriller, fantasy, and horror, plus vertical drama viewing. Community-validated narratives are measured through read rates, micro-transactions, and engagement, then graduate into vertical-drama production and licensable intellectual property — a "story IP engine." KAMI is a consumer product (2.5M+ users) with no public developer API; it is part of the wearekami.com ecosystem and a 500 Global Creators Ventures portfolio company, added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Massive Dynamic
providers.description: Massive Dynamic is an AI-powered advertising platform that bills itself as "The Advertising Copilot" and "the human-AI interface for massive scale." It helps media and advertising teams coordinate large-scale digital ad campaigns by pairing an AI Analysis Copilot (automating daily analytics checks, quarterly business reviews, and Media Mix Modeling) with Execution Delegation, where an AI agent handles operational campaign setup so strategists can focus on decisions. The tool works inside existing Slack and email workflows as a conduit between strategy and activation teams, and emphasizes enterprise-grade data governance with ring-fenced customer data and an explicit commitment not to use customer data to train or improve models. Founded in Paris in 2025 by Trystan Chabert (formerly Head of Growth at Voodoo) and Guillaume le Roy (formerly Head of Engineering at Qonto), the company raised a roughly EUR 3M pre-seed led by Seedcamp in July 2025, with Founders Future, Kima Ventures and others participating, and is deployed with a select group of early design partners. It sells its product as an end-user application — the marketing site is a Figma Sites page whose only call to action is "Request a demo", and the product itself is a login-gated web app at app.massive-dynamic.ai. As of the 2026-08-12 enrichment pass Massive Dynamic publishes no public API, no developer documentation, no SDKs, and no machine-readable contract of any kind — every OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP, agent-card and /.well-known/ probe against its marketing, API and app hosts returned 404 or an application shell.

providers.name: imyup
providers.description: imyup (imyup.com) is a WordPress-powered content website publishing how-to guides, reviews, and download articles focused on mobile gaming (PUBG Mobile, GTA, FIFA, racing and bike games) alongside jobs and general-information posts. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Slow Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this pass the public site exposes no API, developer portal, or programmatic surface; the only machine-readable artifacts discovered are an auto-generated llms.txt and a public XML sitemap. This profile remains a content publication rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Ranker
providers.description: Ranker is a consumer internet company that runs ranker.com, a crowdsourced ranking and voting platform where users vote on and create rankings across pop culture, entertainment, film, TV, music, food, sports, and other consumer topics. Its business arm licenses "Ranker Insights" audience-intelligence and opinion-graph data - drawn from more than 1.5 billion votes, 115 million voters, and 260,000 rankings - to brands, agencies, publishers, and for AI/LLM training. Ranker does not publish a public, self-serve developer API; a private api.ranker.com powers the site and its robots.txt prohibits automated scraping and AI/LLM training use. Data access is sales-led via business.ranker.com. Backed by Bullpen Capital and DCVC.

providers.name: Aiva
providers.description: AIVA (Artificial Intelligence Virtual Artist) is an AI music generation platform that composes original music across more than 250 styles in seconds. Musicians, content creators, and studios generate tracks from prompts or from uploaded audio and MIDI influences, build custom style models, edit the resulting compositions, and export to MP3, MIDI, and WAV. Paid plans add higher download limits, longer tracks, social monetization rights, and full copyright ownership. AIVA is a consumer- and creator-facing product; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery documents.

providers.name: CreatorDAO
providers.description: CreatorDAO supports content creators through funding, bespoke tooling, and training, backing a roster of YouTube and social channels ranging from tens of thousands to millions of subscribers. It operates a decentralized autonomous organization model with an on-chain creator token, promoting its creator app (district.xyz) and community channels rather than a developer platform. Surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and Initialized Capital, CreatorDAO publishes no public API, developer documentation, or API specifications as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: DivX, Inc. (NasdaqGS:DIVX)
providers.description: DivX is a San Diego-based digital video technology company best known for the DivX video codec and format. Under the former public company DivX, Inc. (NasdaqGS:DIVX), and today as DivX, LLC, it offers free and premium consumer software — DivX Software and DivX Pro for Windows and macOS — for playing, converting, and casting video, alongside a technology-licensing business that certifies DivX and HEVC playback in consumer electronics devices (the "DivX Certified" program). The company distributes desktop applications to end users and licenses codecs and playback technology to device manufacturers rather than operating a public developer API platform. Customer support is handled through a Zendesk help center, and enterprise/device partners are served via a Salesforce-based partner portal.

providers.name: FloSports
providers.description: FloSports is an Austin, Texas-based direct-to-consumer sports media and live-streaming company founded in 2006 by brothers Martin and Mark Floreani. It operates a network of vertical properties (FloWrestling, FloTrack, FloGrappling, FloRacing, FloHockey, FloRugby, FloFootball and more) that deliver live and on-demand event streaming, original programming, news, rankings, and results for underserved and passionate sports communities through a subscription model. FloSports surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures; enrichment probing found a consumer streaming site with no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI, well-known discovery documents, or SDK program at this time.

providers.name: Viki
providers.description: Viki (Rakuten Viki) is a global video streaming service specializing in Korean dramas, Chinese dramas, and other Asian television shows and movies, subtitled into more than 200 languages by a community of volunteer contributors (the name is a portmanteau of "video" and "wiki"). Founded as a startup backed by 500 Global, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), and CRV, Viki was acquired by Rakuten in 2013 and now operates as part of Rakuten's media portfolio. The consumer product streams licensed content on web, mobile, and connected-TV apps, funded by advertising and a Viki Pass subscription. Viki does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; it exposes an internal application API (api.viki.io) that powers its own clients and requires app credentials, and a community contribution platform for volunteer subtitlers and segmenters. This profile was surfaced as a venture-portfolio lead and enriched with the honest finding that there is no public API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Discovery Communications
providers.description: Discovery Communications was a global media company providing original and purchased programming across multiple distribution platforms before merging with WarnerMedia in 2022 to form Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD), a leading global media and entertainment company whose portfolio spans HBO Max, Discovery Channel, CNN, Warner Bros. film studios, DC, Food Network, HGTV, and other television, film, and streaming brands. No public developer APIs are documented at the corporate level; technical and partnership inquiries are handled at the individual brand or business-unit level.

providers.name: Headgum
providers.description: Headgum is an American comedy podcast network founded in 2015 by Marty Michael, Amir Blumenfeld, and Jake Hurwitz, with studios in Los Angeles and New York. It produces and distributes premium comedy and entertainment podcasts including Doughboys, Not Another D&D Podcast, Dead Eyes, Hey Riddle Riddle, and Why Won't You Date Me?, and operates Gumball, a host-read podcast and YouTube advertising marketplace that lets brands buy ads directly from creators. Headgum is a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; as of this pass Headgum publishes no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Playback
providers.description: Playback (playback.tv) is a mobile-first live streaming platform backed by Khosla Ventures, where creators broadcast live streams, audiences watch and interact in real time, and streamers earn through the platform's monetization program. The consumer product is organized around streaming, watching, earning, and community guidelines. As of this enrichment pass Playback publishes a consumer web/app experience and a Notaku-powered help center but exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or documented developer surface; this profile therefore carries identity and domain-security signal only.

providers.name: Audio Up Media
providers.description: Audio Up Media is a Los Angeles based podcast studio, music company and audio entertainment network founded in 2020 by Jared Gutstadt, the founder of Jingle Punks. The company develops and produces scripted and unscripted audio series, original music IP and branded audio campaigns, and adapts that intellectual property into television, film and live formats. Its catalog includes scripted titles such as Strawberry Spring, Make It Up As We Go, Where the Bodies Are Buried and Maejor Frequency, alongside branded case-study work for consumer brands. Audio Up is a content studio rather than a software platform: it publishes a marketing site and distributes its shows through third-party podcast platforms, and does not operate a developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable specification of its own.

providers.name: Callisto Media
providers.description: Callisto Media Inc. was a data-driven nonfiction book publisher founded in 2011 by chief executive Benjamin Wayne, operating from 1955 Broadway in Oakland, California (earlier Emeryville) and 220 West 19th Street in New York. It built a publishing model around demand signals rather than editorial instinct — mining point-of-sale data, search volume and category gaps to decide which instructional titles to commission, then matching each topic to a subject-matter author. Its primary imprint was Rockridge Press, best known for diet-, appliance- and condition-specific cookbooks and health titles, alongside the Callisto Kids line of pre-K through grade 12 workbooks, STEM, history and biography titles; the company said it had reached more than 50 million customers and ranked among the top fifteen US publishers by unit sales. It raised venture funding from 137 Ventures in 2017, then contracted sharply — cutting 35 percent of staff in July 2022 and a further 200 roles that October — and on 9 May 2023 its publishing assets were acquired by the independent publisher Sourcebooks in a deal funded by Penguin Random House, with Simon & Schuster Distribution Services continuing to distribute the titles. The brand now trades as Callisto Publishing, a Sourcebooks imprint: callistomedia.com 301-redirects to callistopublishing.com, which 301-redirects again to sourcebooks.com/callisto (chain verified 2026-08-02). Callisto Media is a consumer publishing business, not a software vendor, and has no public API surface. Probes on 2026-08-02 against callistomedia.com, www.callistopublishing.com and www.sourcebooks.com returned no machine-readable contract: /openapi.json, /swagger.json and /.well-known/ai-plugin.json all 404, /.well-known/agent-card.json and /.well-known/agent.json both 404 (no A2A agent card), and every other probed path answered with the Sourcebooks single-page Magento storefront shell rather than a document. There is no developer portal, no GitHub organization (callistomedia, callisto-media and rockridgepress all 404 on the GitHub API), no published SDK on npm or PyPI, and no llms.txt.

providers.name: Circle of Moms
providers.description: Circle of Moms was an online community for mothers, organized around topical mom groups, discussion threads and mom blogs, covering pregnancy, babies and infants, parenting and family health. It is a portfolio company of Uncork Capital (formerly SoftTech VC) and was later operated under the POPSUGAR brand, whose branding appears on archived captures of the site. The service is no longer operating: the circleofmoms.com domain is still registered but now redirects to the POPSUGAR Family page on Facebook, and its DNS is administered under Vox Media, POPSUGAR's parent. Circle of Moms never published a public API, developer portal, or partner platform — web-archive crawls of the domain contain no developer, API-documentation, or OAuth paths, and no developer or api subdomain has ever been recorded. This profile is retained as a historical company record with no API surface.

providers.name: DIVE studios
providers.description: DIVE Studios is a global K-entertainment media platform that produces original shows, podcasts, and short-form social content, reaching over 135M Gen Z and Millennial fans and 5B+ lifetime views. The company operates two commercial arms: DIVE Media, which sells advertising and branded content across its podcast, video, and social network, and DIVE Agency (DIVE X), which builds creator, influencer, and celebrity marketing campaigns for global brands connecting with K-culture audiences. It publishes an llms.txt describing its pages but exposes no public developer API, SDK, or portal. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Hungama
providers.description: Hungama (Hungama Digital Media Entertainment Pvt. Ltd.) is an Indian digital entertainment company operating a video-on-demand and audio OTT platform. Hungama.com offers trending web series, popular movies, Hungama Originals, music, podcasts, audiobooks, and audio stories across Hindi, Bollywood, Punjabi, and regional Indian content. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Hungama publishes a public LLM Access Policy (llms.txt) governing how AI systems may crawl, summarize, and reference its content, but exposes no public developer API or documentation.

providers.name: Kobalt Music
providers.description: Kobalt Music Group is a music services company providing publishing administration, neighbouring rights and recordings services for songwriters, artists, publishers and rights holders. It collects, matches and accounts for royalties across streaming and digital platforms, reporting to clients through its own portals rather than a public developer program. Kobalt's rights and content management platform is operated by KTech, its technology arm, which processes the micro-transaction royalty data behind Kobalt Music Publishing and AMRA, the global digital collection society. As of the July 2026 enrichment pass Kobalt publishes no public API, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification; the only public machine-readable surface found was an RFC 9116 security.txt.

providers.name: Light Chaser Animation Studios
providers.description: Light Chaser Animation Studios (追光动画) is a Chinese computer-animation film studio founded in March 2013 by Gary Wang (王微), founder and former CEO of the video platform Tudou, and headquartered in Beijing. The studio produces original CG animated feature films for the Chinese domestic market, drawing on Chinese mythology, literature and history. Its released titles include Little Door Gods (小门神), Tea Pets (阿唐奇遇), Cats and Peachtopia (猫与桃花源), White Snake (白蛇：缘起), New Gods: Nezha Reborn (新神榜：哪吒重生), White Snake 2: Green Snake (白蛇2：青蛇劫起), New Gods: Yang Jian (新神榜：杨戬) and Chang An (长安三万里). Light Chaser is a film-production company rather than a technology vendor: its public web presence is a bilingual WordPress marketing and recruiting site at zhuiguang.com, and as of this enrichment pass it publishes no developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts of any kind.

providers.name: Stats Perform
providers.description: Stats Perform is a global sports data, AI, and technology company formed by the 2019 merger of Stats LLC and the Perform Group. The company owns and operates the Opta brand, the de facto standard for granular football (soccer) event data, and supplies live data, advanced metrics, predictive models, video, graphics, and AI-powered content to media broadcasters, sportsbooks, fantasy operators, professional clubs, leagues, governing bodies, and brands. Its product portfolio is organised around three customer segments — Media & Tech, Betting & Fantasy, and Team Performance — and exposes data and AI capabilities through a family of Opta-branded products including Opta Feeds (XML/JSON sports data feeds), Opta Live (live event data), Opta Stream (low-latency push), Opta Vision (computer-vision tracking), Opta Predictions (probability models), Opta Points (player ratings), Opta Pulse (event commentary), Opta Stories (auto-generated narratives), Opta Search (natural-language sports search), Opta Graphics (broadcast graphics), and OptaAI Studio (AI content tooling). Access to Opta data and APIs is partner-gated: prospective customers must contract through Stats Perform sales, and developer documentation, schemas, and reference material are delivered through a private customer portal rather than a public developer area. Stats Perform also operates StatsBomb's competitors The Analyst as a public-facing editorial property, and runs the annual Opta Forum for customers and analysts.

providers.name: TPP GROUP INC.
providers.description: TPP Group is a media intelligence company that creates and scales Arabic content, helping brands make data-driven marketing investments across the Arabic-speaking world. It operates four integrated divisions - Network (Arabic intellectual property development, 40+ owned and operated IPs), Studio (production infrastructure with 1,400+ produced episodes), Agency (performance-driven distribution), and Intelligence (psychographic audience-behavior analytics and attention measurement). A 500 Global portfolio company; it publishes no public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Upthere
providers.description: Upthere was a consumer cloud-storage company backed by GV and founded by former Apple software engineering chief Bertrand Serlet. Its Upthere Home app was designed as "one home" for photos, videos, music, and documents, stored directly in the Upthere cloud with fast search, private sharing, and shared "Loops". Western Digital acquired Upthere in 2017 and later discontinued the service; upthere.com now 302-redirects every path to a retired Western Digital support notice. Upthere never published a public developer API, and no API surface remains — this profile records the company identity and the posture of the surviving domain.

providers.name: UTURN
providers.description: UTURN Entertainment is a Saudi Arabian digital media and entertainment company founded in 2010 that has grown into the largest Arabic Multi-Channel Network (MCN) in the MENA region. It produces original digital content — comedy sketches, gaming (Saudi Gamer), women's lifestyle (Unseen), sports (MLM), and MMA (MMAnia) shows — distributed across YouTube, TikTok, Snapchat, and other social platforms, and offers content creation, sponsored content, branded content, and digital production services to brands. A 500 Global portfolio company, UTURN publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: Adim
providers.description: Adim is an entertainment-technology and web3 media company co-founded in 2022 by It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia creator Rob McElhenney alongside Richard Rosenblatt, Chase Rosenblatt, Melissa Kaspers, and Spencer Marell. Adim invites a community of storytellers, writers, and fans to collaboratively create, develop, and co-own a new generation of intellectual property — stories, characters, and narrative universes known as the Adimverse — rewarding contributors with ownership stakes and a say in how the community is governed. The company raised a $5M seed round led by Chris Dixon of a16z crypto. Adim is a consumer creative platform rather than an API provider; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Catalog
providers.description: Catalog was a music distribution and direct-to-fan platform that let independent musicians sell digital downloads while keeping 100% of earnings, collect fan emails directly, split revenue with collaborators, run referral rewards, and control private, public, or scheduled releases with zero marketplace fees. The company has ceased operations - its homepage now shows a closure announcement - and it never published a public developer API, SDKs, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Liberty Interactive
providers.description: Liberty Interactive Corporation owned and operated a broad range of video and online commerce companies, including QVC, HSN, and zulily, before being reorganized into Qurate Retail Group in 2018. The corporation tracked separate operating units through Liberty Interactive Group and Liberty Ventures Group tracking stocks.

providers.name: Liberty Media
providers.description: Liberty Media Corporation is a media and entertainment holding company headquartered in Englewood, Colorado, owning interests in a portfolio of assets across media, entertainment, and sports. Its primary holding is the Formula One Group, which encompasses Formula 1 racing operations and MotoGP motorcycle racing, alongside investments in companies such as Liberty Broadband, QVC Group, Atlanta Braves Holdings, and Liberty Live Holdings.

providers.name: Massive Science
providers.description: Massive Science is a science communication platform and media company that publishes stories, explainers, lab notes, and reports about current research, written and edited by working scientists. It runs the Massive Science Consortium, a training network of scientist-writers, alongside editorial content, newsletters, a community discussion forum, and a shop. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment finds no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable interface beyond a public RSS feed.

providers.name: Podfund
providers.description: Podfund provides startup and growth capital to podcast creators and audio-driven media companies, typically investing $25,000 to $150,000 based on stage, track record, traction, and revenue. Operated by TechNexus Venture Collaborative, which has backed 600+ startups since 2007, Podfund pairs funding with business planning, a peer community, mentor matching, a growth toolkit, and partner offers. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta and added to the API Evangelist network. Podfund publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile captures its identity and web presence for network discovery.

providers.name: Emergent VR *
providers.description: Emergent VR was a San Francisco Bay Area virtual-reality startup backed by GV (Google Ventures), where it is listed in the portfolio with the asterisk GV uses to mark exited companies. The enrichment pass found no live company web presence: the former emergentvr.com domain now resolves to an unrelated third-party blog, and the company's GitHub organization (github.com/EmergentVR, created March 2015) holds only ten repositories, all of them OpenCV builds and a fork of Google's cardboard-unity SDK, with no activity after June 2016. No developer portal, documentation, API, SDK, or event surface exists for this company, so no API artifacts were produced. Sector: consumer / virtual reality.

providers.name: Fanbread
providers.description: Fanbread is a defunct venture-backed company originally surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. Its primary domain fanbread.com no longer resolves to a live site — the HTTPS handshake fails and HTTP returns 410 Gone from a parking host — and no website, developer portal, documentation, API reference, or machine-readable API surface remains anywhere. The company's GitHub organization survives under the login FanBread but is now titled "Wild Sky Media FnB" and points at wildskymedia.com; its seven public repositories are forks and small front-end utilities with no first-party API artifacts and no activity since April 2020. This profile is retained as a historical record and a dead-domain marker, not as an active API provider.

providers.name: Inkitt
providers.description: Inkitt is a data-driven storytelling and self-publishing technology company that runs a reading and writing community (inkitt.com) and the paid serialized-fiction reading app Galatea. It uses reader-engagement analytics and algorithms to discover promising manuscripts from independent authors and develop the most popular into commercial fiction and adaptations across its Inkitt and Galatea platforms. Founded in 2013 and backed by Earlybird, HV Capital, Khosla Ventures, Kleiner Perkins and Speedinvest, Inkitt operates consumer mobile and web reading products rather than a public developer API; this profile tracks its public web, domain-security, and GitHub surface.

providers.name: Mobcrush
providers.description: Mobcrush Streaming, Inc. was a Santa Monica, California live-streaming technology company, founded in 2013 by Royce Disini with James Hurley, Travis Rogers and Stephen Dao, that made it possible for mobile gamers to broadcast gameplay straight from an iOS or Android device with no capture card, no desktop encoder and no third-party software. Its differentiator was simulcast: a creator went live once and Mobcrush relayed the same broadcast simultaneously to Twitch, YouTube, Facebook, Twitter and Periscope at no extra charge, which turned the product from a competing destination into distribution infrastructure for creators who already had audiences elsewhere. The company added an advertising and sponsorship layer in 2018 ("Go Live, Get Paid") and operated Mineville, one of six official Minecraft server partners under agreement with Microsoft, reaching more than twenty million players a year. It raised roughly $35.9M across its rounds, including an $11M Series A in September 2015 led by Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers and a $20M round in 2016, with First Round Capital and Lowercase Capital also participating. Super League Gaming announced its acquisition of Mobcrush on 11 March 2021 and closed it on 2 June 2021 for approximately 12.6 million shares of common stock; the acquirer now trades as Super League Enterprise, Inc. and does not carry the Mobcrush brand forward as a product. Mobcrush ran a JSON web API at www.mobcrush.com/api/ that backed its own site and mobile apps, but it never published a developer portal, an API reference, a first-party SDK or any machine-readable specification, so there is no public API surface to catalog — and the mobcrush.com domain, while still registered, no longer resolves at all. This profile is retained as a historical record.

providers.name: Movielala
providers.description: MovieLaLa Inc was a San Francisco movie-discovery and social-video startup (500 Global portfolio, founded 2012) best known for its GIF maker and a MovieLaLa Video Player. The only developer surface it ever published was a client-side JavaScript embed API for that player (a drop-in replacement for the YouTube IFrame API, loaded from assets-embed.movielala.com), documented in the github.com/movielala GitHub org. The company is now defunct — its last public code activity was 2016 and the gif-maker repo redirects to gifmaker.io. The movielala.com domain has lapsed and is currently repurposed by an unrelated third party (an Indonesian gambling site), so it no longer represents the company and is not wired as a website here. No REST/OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, or hosted API surface exists to enrich.

providers.name: NBC
providers.description: NBC (National Broadcasting Company) is a major American commercial broadcast television network and a subsidiary of Comcast through NBCUniversal. NBC produces news (NBC News, Today), entertainment, late-night, and sports programming (Sunday Night Football, Olympic Games). NBC and parent company NBCUniversal do not publish a public developer portal. Programmatic advertising APIs (NBCUniversal One Platform) and streaming partner integrations (Peacock) are offered only through direct sales relationships rather than self-serve developer signup.

providers.name: Paramount
providers.description: Paramount is a global media and entertainment company producing premium content and experiences for audiences worldwide, encompassing film, television, and streaming through brands such as Paramount Pictures, CBS, Nickelodeon, MTV, Comedy Central, BET, Paramount+, and Pluto TV.

providers.name: The Athletic
providers.description: The Athletic is a subscription-based digital sports media company founded in 2016 by Alex Mather and Adam Hansmann, offering in-depth, ad-light coverage of national and local professional and college sports through a large staff of beat writers and columnists. Acquired by The New York Times Company in 2022, The Athletic delivers written articles, newsletters, podcasts, and live coverage across its website and mobile apps. As of this enrichment pass The Athletic does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications; its GitHub organization contains only forks of open-source engineering tooling rather than any public API product.

providers.name: Tally Labs
providers.description: Tally Labs is a Web3 media and entertainment company founded in 2021 and headquartered in the United States. It is best known for creating and operating Jenkins the Valet, a fictional character and NFT project built around Bored Ape Yacht Club #1798, and for the community-generative NFT novel "Bored & Dangerous," set in the fictional world of Azurbala and written with New York Times bestselling author Neil Strauss. The company builds characters, narratives, and interactive storytelling tools intended to let creators turn their imaginations into content. Tally Labs raised a $12M seed round in May 2022 led by a16z crypto. As a Web3 media/IP company it does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications; this profile captures its identity and public web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: 1 Mainstream
providers.description: 1 Mainstream was a cloud-based OTT (over-the-top) video streaming platform for content owners and distributors, enabling operators to launch live and on-demand video services across connected devices including iOS, Android, Roku, Amazon Fire TV, Chromecast, game consoles, smart TVs, and Apple TV, with DRM (Widevine, PlayReady), multi-CDN control, subscriber management, entitlements, and a CMS-based analytics engine. Backed by Sky and DCM Ventures, the company was acquired by Cisco in October 2015 and folded into Cisco's Infinite Video suite of cloud-powered video entertainment solutions. The standalone 1mainstream.com domain no longer resolves; this profile is retained as a historical portfolio-lead record.

providers.name: 555 Comic
providers.description: 555 Comic is an interactive storytelling and virtual-influencer studio founded by Ben Watanabe. It runs casts of anime-styled virtual characters — such as @CRC_Luna — who publish real-time alternate-reality-game (ARG) stories across TikTok, Twitter/X and Instagram, letting fans create original characters (OCs) and interact with official storylines across four interconnected fictional worlds: Conspiracy Research Club, All Night Arcade, The Convenience Store, and a Paranormal Research Club. Stories unfold in real time on "Poppy-valley Standard Time," with fans participating through social comments. 555 Comic is a Techstars Music portfolio company. It publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface; this profile captures its identity and a domain-security probe of its web host.

providers.name: 60dB
providers.description: 60dB was a personalized short-form audio and podcast application built by Tiny Garage Labs, founded in 2016 by John Ciancutti, Steve Henn, and Steve McLendon. The app curated and recommended short radio-style audio stories tailored to a listener's habits, and was available on iOS, Android, and the web as well as through Alexa, Android Auto, and CarPlay. It was backed by Bloomberg Beta, Khosla Ventures, and Rivet Ventures. Google acqui-hired the founding team in October 2017 and the 60dB service was shut down on November 10, 2017. The company is defunct and publishes no developer program, API, or machine-readable interface today; the 60db.com domain now resolves to a parked placeholder page. This profile is retained as a historical portfolio-company record for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: 88rising
providers.description: 88rising (stylized 88 with a rising arrow) is an American mass media company and record label founded in 2015 by Sean Miyashiro, headquartered in Los Angeles and New York with a division in Shanghai. It describes itself as a hybrid management, record label, video production and marketing company, and is known for building a global platform for Asian and Asian American artists including Rich Brian, NIKI, Joji and Keith Ape. Beyond recorded music it operates the Head in the Clouds festival franchise and the 88 Night Market live and commerce brand. It is a media and entertainment company rather than a software company: it publishes no developer program, no public API documentation and no machine-readable specifications.

providers.name: Absurd
providers.description: Absurd is an AI video creation platform positioning itself as "the Creative OS for AI video." It uses autonomous AI agents to handle scripting, scene planning, and video generation, letting companies produce brand and performance advertisements at scale in roughly 72 hours instead of weeks. Based in Los Angeles and part of Y Combinator's Fall 2025 batch, Absurd works with brands such as Hims, Kalshi, Replit, Brex, Whop, and Reforge, with some of its generated videos reaching over a million organic views. The company runs a managed, sales-led production motion rather than a self-serve platform: its published sitemap declares exactly four routes (home, portfolio, careers, contact), and it ships no pricing page, no blog, no developer portal, no documentation, no SDKs, and no GitHub organization. Three Absurd-controlled hosts are live but none is a developer surface — app.absurd.com is the gated customer application, api.absurd.com is its private FastAPI backend with schema and docs routes disabled, and lp.absurd.com is a key-gated Supabase project serving the landing page. This entry was enriched from public web sources and live unauthenticated probes, and will be upgraded if a developer surface appears.

providers.name: All Def Digital
providers.description: All Def (formerly All Def Digital) is a YouTube-focused digital content studio founded by Russell Simmons that produces unscripted original programming for Gen Z, Millennial, and multicultural audiences across comedy, food, hip-hop, and culture. Its owned-and-operated channels have amassed 15M+ fans and more than 2 billion video views, and it produces branded content for partners including Sprite, Snickers, Hyundai, Lexus, and McDonald's. All Def is a portfolio company of a16z, surfaced in the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, documentation, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Anchor *
providers.description: Anchor was a podcast creation, hosting, distribution, and monetization platform (anchor.fm), founded in 2015 and backed by GV (Google Ventures) among others. Spotify acquired Anchor in 2019 and folded it into its creator tooling, later rebranding the product to Spotify for Podcasters and then Spotify for Creators. The anchor.fm domain now 302-redirects to Spotify's creator product (podcasters.spotify.com / creators.spotify.com); Anchor never published a standalone public developer API, and it no longer operates as an independent company. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of gv and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub lead; enrichment confirms it is an acquired/absorbed brand with no independent developer surface to harvest.

providers.name: Anchor FM
providers.description: Anchor FM was a podcast creation, hosting, distribution, and monetization platform founded in 2015 that let anyone record, edit, publish, and monetize a podcast for free from a phone or browser. Spotify acquired Anchor in 2019 and folded the product into Spotify for Podcasters, later rebranded Spotify for Creators; the anchor.fm domain now redirects to creators.spotify.com. Anchor never published a public developer API or developer portal, so this API Evangelist profile carries company identity and domain-security posture only. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel (consumer sector).

providers.name: Associated Content
providers.description: Associated Content was an open content publishing platform founded in 2005 by Luke Beatty that paid contributors to publish articles, video, audio, and images on any topic, then distributed that library through associatedcontent.com and a network of syndication partners. At its peak it hosted over one million pieces of content from roughly 250,000 contributors and adopted Thomson Reuters OpenCalais for automated classification of that library. It raised a $5.4M Series A from SoftBank Capital (2006), a $10M Series B from SoftBank, Canaan Partners, and Tim Armstrong (2007), and $6M more in 2009, before Yahoo acquired it in May 2010. Yahoo rebranded the property as Yahoo Voices in December 2011 and shut it down on July 31, 2014, retiring the Yahoo Contributor Network the following month. The company is defunct: it never published a public developer API, and associatedcontent.com is now a parked domain that refuses HTTPS.

providers.name: Auditude
providers.description: Auditude was a Palo Alto video advertising technology company founded in 2007 that let premium publishers, content owners and media companies manage, serve and monetize advertising around online video across multiple platforms and devices via its proprietary Auditude Connect platform. Backed by Redpoint Ventures and Greylock Partners with roughly $38M raised, its customers included Comcast, Sony Music and Universal Music Group. Adobe acquired Auditude in November 2011 for a reported ~$120M and folded the technology into Adobe Primetime (ad decisioning / ad insertion), since rebranded under Adobe Pass. Auditude no longer operates as an independent company: auditude.com does not resolve, and the only surviving public footprint is the legacy com.auditude.ads.* namespace inside Adobe's Primetime Player SDK documentation. This profile is retained as a defunct / acquired historical record; there is no Auditude API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Beast Industries
providers.description: Beast Industries is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of social-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: creator-economy. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Beek
providers.description: Beek was a Spanish-language audiobook and ebook streaming platform serving Latin America and Spain, backed by Accel and Lightspeed Venture Partners. At its peak it reached over 4 million users who streamed nearly 200 million minutes of audio content, including its exclusive Beek Originals catalog. The service has since shut down: Amazon's Audible acquired a significant portion of the Beek Originals catalog, and Beek now redirects listeners to Audible to continue their libraries. Beek ran a private backend service (api.beek.io) but published no public developer program, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer documentation, so it has no consumable API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Buzzer
providers.description: Buzzer was a mobile live-sports streaming startup founded in 2020 by Bo Han, formerly director of live content at Twitter. Its consumer app, launched in 2021, sold micropayment access — as low as $0.99 to $1 — to short in-game moments of live sporting events, targeting Gen Z fans who would not buy a full cable or league subscription. Buzzer secured streaming rights covering the NBA, WNBA, NHL, PGA Tour and ATP Tour, and raised roughly $44 million in total, including a $20 million Series A in June 2021 co-led by Sapphire Sport and Canaan Partners alongside a large group of athlete and team-owner investors. On 19 May 2023 the company shut down the direct-to-consumer app and pivoted to a business-to-business model branded "Powered by Buzzer", announced as API licensing, custom development and consulting for leagues, teams and networks streaming direct to fans. That offering never reached public availability: Buzzer ceased all operations on 30 June 2023, citing "recent fundraising developments and market dynamics". No public developer portal, API documentation, specification, SDK or package was ever published. The buzzer.com domain no longer hosts the company and now redirects to an Atom.com domain-for-sale listing. Retained in the network as a historical record of a defunct company; not an active API provider.

providers.name: Callin
providers.description: Callin was a social podcasting and live-streaming platform founded by David Sacks and Axel Ericsson, backed by Craft Ventures, that let creators stream live audio, take listener questions, then record, edit, publish and share the result as a podcast episode. The company was acquired by Rumble (NASDAQ: RUM) in May 2023 and the standalone consumer app was subsequently wound down. As of enrichment the callin.com domain returns only a Cloudflare-gated placeholder and the provider exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDK surface to enrich.

providers.name: chushou
providers.description: Chushou (触手TV / 触手直播) was a China-based mobile game live-streaming platform, at one point among the largest mobile-focused game streaming services in China, letting players broadcast and watch mobile gameplay. It was backed by Qiming Venture Partners and Tencent and is surfaced here as a portfolio lead. As of this enrichment pass the company's public web presence at chushou.tv is unreachable (the server returns empty replies) and it exposes no documented developer API, SDK, or portal, so this profile remains an inactive/defunct lead with no live API surface to enrich beyond DNS/TLS-level signals.

providers.name: Chute
providers.description: Chute was a visual marketing automation platform (getchute.com) that helped brands discover, collect, rights-manage and publish consumer and user-generated visual content. Its product line spanned visual insights, digital asset management and content publishing, and it exposed a public REST API documented on Apiary (docs.chute.apiary.io) with first-party Ruby and Node.js client libraries. The company is defunct: the canonical domain no longer serves a site, the API and developer hosts do not resolve, the Apiary documentation returns 502, and the github.com/chute organization has been deleted. Only the abandoned package-registry entries survive. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical record of a former API provider.

providers.name: Conteller
providers.description: Conteller is a user-generated content (UGC) marketplace where brands pay for authentic media directly from their own customers and everyday, non-famous creators. Brands publish media briefs and the platform lets creators capture, submit, and store photos, videos, and TikTok-style content, then handles paying those creators for approved submissions. A Mexican/Spanish startup (Madrid) selected for Batch 19 of 500 Global's Somos Lucha accelerator program in Latin America, Conteller has run pilots spanning roughly 1,400 creators and a dozen brands. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead of 500 Global. The public site is no longer serving: conteller.com and www.conteller.com both return HTTP 402 "Payment required / DEPLOYMENT_DISABLED" from Vercel on every path, the blog subdomain returns a Cloudflare 1014 and the admin subdomain a 522, and the Internet Archive holds no successful capture of the site after 2025-07-16. No public developer portal, API, documentation, OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP or agent-card surface has ever been found for Conteller, and its GitHub organization publishes no repositories.

providers.name: Curio Labs
providers.description: Curio (curio.io), operated by Curio Labs, was a London-based audio-journalism subscription app founded in 2016 by Govind Balakrishnan and Srikant Chakravarti. It turned articles from premium publishers into professionally narrated audio and later added AI-generated personalized episodes. Backed by 500 Global (formerly 500 Startups), EarlyBird, Draper Esprit, Cherry Ventures and Horizons Ventures, it raised over $15M before the founders wound the company down after eight years, citing AI and big-tech competition; they have since moved on to a new venture (Gibran). Enrichment probe finds no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface — curio.io now serves a closure/landing page only.

providers.name: Deep Render
providers.description: Deep Render is an artificial-intelligence company that developed neural-network-based ("learned") video and image compression technology, aiming to replace traditional hand-engineered codecs such as H.264/HEVC/AV1 with deep-learning models for higher compression efficiency. Founded as a London-based startup, it was backed by Speedinvest and was surfaced into the API Evangelist network through VC-portfolio discovery. As of this enrichment pass its primary domain, deeprender.ai, issues a blanket HTTP 301 redirect to InterDigital's Video Lab (https://www.interdigital.com/video-lab/), indicating the company and its compression technology have been absorbed into InterDigital. Deep Render publishes no independent developer portal, API, documentation, SDK, or other machine-readable surface for enrichment at this time.

providers.name: Dubsmash
providers.description: Dubsmash was a video-selfie and lip-sync mobile application that let users record short videos set to a library of popular audio clips, quotes, and songs. Founded in Germany in 2014 by Jonas Druppel, Roland Grenke, and Daniel Taschik, it grew into one of the most downloaded social video apps, particularly among younger creators in the United States. Reddit acquired Dubsmash in December 2020, integrated its video-creation technology into the Reddit platform, and discontinued the standalone Dubsmash app on February 22, 2022. Dubsmash never offered a public developer API, SDK, or documentation program; its consumer domain (dubsmash.com) no longer resolves. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical, defunct company record surfaced from venture-capital portfolio data.

providers.name: edisn.ai
providers.description: edisn.ai was an AI-powered fan engagement platform for sports and media, surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. The enrichment pipeline found no public developer surface — no API, OpenAPI, SDK, package, or documentation, and no docs/developer/api subdomain ever archived. The domain expired on 2026-05-09 and is now in pendingDelete/clientHold with no DNS resolution; by 2024 it already redirected to fubo.tv. No provider artifacts could be captured because none exist to search or derive from.

providers.name: Endeavor
providers.description: Endeavor was a global sports and entertainment company representing talent and owning and operating events, with subsidiaries including WME, IMG, and UFC. Following the 2024 take-private transaction by Silver Lake and the separation of TKO Group Holdings (UFC and WWE), the remaining talent, media, marketing, and licensing businesses were rebranded as WME Group. This repository tracks Endeavor as a corporate entity; no public developer APIs are currently published.

providers.name: Endeavor Group Holdings
providers.description: Endeavor Group Holdings was a global sports and entertainment company that represented talent, owned and operated events, and provided licensing, marketing, and media services through subsidiaries including WME, IMG, and UFC. Following the 2024 take-private transaction by Silver Lake and the separation of TKO Group Holdings (UFC and WWE), the remaining talent representation, media, marketing, and licensing businesses were rebranded as WME Group, which now operates WME, 160over90, Pantheon Media Group, and IMG Licensing. No public developer APIs are currently published.

providers.name: EST
providers.description: EST (EST Media) is a Los Angeles-based media holding company founded by Jaeson Ma and Eric Tu that amplifies Asian stories and talent for global audiences. It operates three divisions: EST Studios, which develops, finances, produces, and sells Asian film and television projects; Eastern Standard Times, a Gen Z digital video platform sharing untold stories from Asia and its diaspora; and Established, a content studio partnering with global brands on advertising campaigns, influencer collaborations, commercials, and experiential events. EST Media is a 500 Global portfolio company. It publishes no public API or developer platform; this profile carries company identity and a domain-security probe only.

providers.name: Fan Controlled Football
providers.description: Fan Controlled Football (FCF) was a professional indoor American football league in which fans voted on play calls in real time through a mobile app, playing a fast, 7-on-7 format staged at Pullman Yards in Atlanta and streamed to social and live-video audiences. The league drew high-profile athlete and celebrity team owners and investors and positioned itself as a fan-interactive, tech-driven sports and entertainment property. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. FCF paused operations and its public web presence (fcf.io) no longer serves a live site, so it currently exposes no developer portal, documentation, or API surface.

providers.name: Flixster
providers.description: Flixster is an American movie-discovery and social entertainment brand founded in 2007 that let people rate and review movies, browse local showtimes, watch trailers, and share what they were watching. It grew into one of the largest movie communities on the web and mobile, and in 2011 was acquired by Warner Bros. together with Rotten Tomatoes; Fandango Media later acquired both Flixster and Rotten Tomatoes from Warner Bros. in 2016. The Flixster Video digital-locker service (built on UltraViolet) was shut down in 2019. The flixster.com property no longer operates as an independent consumer site — it now redirects to Fandango, and Flixster does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company/brand record; there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Gamefam
providers.description: Gamefam is a gaming studio that builds and operates high-quality branded games and interactive experiences for Gen Z and Gen Alpha audiences on platforms such as Roblox and Fortnite. It develops games, media campaigns, and amplification programs for 50+ brand partners (including LEGO, Adidas, Disney, and Netflix) and runs creator-facing programs such as Dev X and its Creator Fund. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. As of this enrichment pass Gamefam publishes no public developer API, portal, SDK, or OpenAPI surface — its products are consumer game experiences distributed through third-party platforms.

providers.name: Gimme Media
providers.description: Gimme Media is the Techstars-backed music company behind Gimme Radio, the heavy-metal streaming and live-DJ radio platform that later expanded into Gimme Metal and Gimme Country. The standalone streaming apps were wound down, and the brand now operates as a Shopify-hosted storefront at gimmemetal.com selling vinyl, merchandise, and exclusive releases to the metal community. As of this enrichment pass Gimme Media publishes no first-party public developer API, SDKs, OpenAPI definition, or developer documentation; the only machine-readable surfaces served at its domain are the Shopify Customer Accounts platform OIDC endpoints, which belong to the hosting platform rather than to a Gimme Media API.

providers.name: Glow
providers.description: Glow (glow.fm) was a podcast subscription and membership monetization platform that let podcasters run paid, listener-supported premium feeds. The standalone product has since been folded into Libsyn: as of this enrichment pass the glow.fm domain issues a 301 redirect to Libsyn's podcast-monetization offering, its TLS certificate has expired, and no active developer portal, API, documentation, or SDK surface remains under the Glow brand. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead (a16z, Norwest Venture Partners, Union Square Ventures) and has no live API to enrich.

providers.name: Graphicly
providers.description: Graphicly was a digital-comics and e-book distribution and self-publishing platform, founded around 2009 in Austin, Texas, that let independent creators and publishers convert their work and distribute it across major reading platforms including Amazon Kindle, Apple iBooks, Barnes & Noble Nook, and Google Play. Backed by 500 Startups (500 Global) among other investors, the company was acquired by Blurb in 2014 and its distribution service was subsequently discontinued. The graphicly.com domain no longer serves a live product, and the company exposes no public developer portal, documentation, or API surface. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network for portfolio-graph and historical reference; enrichment found no live API, SDK, event, or security surface to harvest.

providers.name: Group Nine Media
providers.description: Group Nine Media was a New York-based digital-media holding company formed in 2016 through the merger of Discovery Digital with the original Group Nine, uniting the news brand NowThis, the animal brand The Dodo, the lifestyle brand Thrillist, and the science brand Seeker under one roof (it later added PopSugar). Backed by Discovery Inc. and venture investor IVP, it built large social-video and branded-content audiences before it was acquired by Vox Media in February 2022 and folded into that portfolio. Group Nine operated as a consumer media publisher, not an API provider: it did not publish a public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or any machine-readable API surface, and its groupnine.com domain now resolves to a third-party domain-sale landing page. This profile is retained as a VC-portfolio identity record with no scorable API artifacts.

providers.name: iHeartMedia
providers.description: iHeartMedia is America's #1 audio company, reaching 9 out of 10 Americans every month through broadcast radio, digital streaming, podcasts, live events, and on-demand entertainment. Public API documentation, developer programs, or open API artifacts have not been identified for iHeartMedia. This repository exists to track APIs, SDKs, and developer resources should they become available.

providers.name: Invisible Universe
providers.description: Invisible Universe is a consumer entertainment company building AI-powered animated intellectual property for social platforms — described by FastCompany as "building the Pixar of the internet one TikTok at a time." It has launched multiple animated franchises reaching millions of followers and billions of views across TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube, and created Invisible Studio, a proprietary AI engine that compresses short-form animated content production from weeks to hours. Backed by Initialized Capital, it operates in the consumer/media sector. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead; as of this pass the company publishes no public developer platform, API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Iyuno
providers.description: Iyuno is one of the world's leading media localization companies, providing dubbing, subtitling, and access services for film, television, and streaming platforms across dozens of languages and markets worldwide. It was formed from the combination of Iyuno Media Group and SDI Media and is backed by the SoftBank Vision Fund. Iyuno operates as an enterprise content and media-services provider; as of this profiling it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API artifacts, so this profile carries company identity only.

providers.name: Jubilee Inc
providers.description: Jubilee Inc (Jubilee Media) is a Los Angeles-based digital media production company that creates discussion-based and dating video shows designed to provoke thoughtful conversation and foster human connection across social and ideological divides. Its flagship YouTube programs include Middle Ground, Odd One Out, and Ranking, alongside sister dating channels such as Love Comma Nectar (Versus 1) and the reaction and behind-the-scenes brand TwoBilee. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes no public API or developer platform at this time, so this profile carries identity and domain-security signal only.

providers.name: Kerning Cultures
providers.description: Kerning Cultures is a Middle East and North Africa media company producing narrative journalism and audio storytelling podcasts in Arabic and English. Based in Dubai, UAE and backed by 500 Global, the Kerning Cultures Network creates original shows, branded audio, and advertising for a regional listener audience. It operates as a consumer media and content brand and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a developer portal; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record awaiting any future API surface.

providers.name: Kuwo Music
providers.description: Kuwo Music (酷我音乐) is a Chinese online music streaming service, founded in Beijing in 2005, that grew from a desktop music player into one of China's major consumer streaming apps across desktop, web, and mobile. Kuwo merged with Kugou under China Music Corporation, which was subsequently acquired by Tencent Music Entertainment Group, and Kuwo now operates as one of TME's music apps alongside QQ Music and Kugou. Kuwo entered the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead via Qiming. It is a consumer-facing streaming property rather than an API-first provider, and no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface has been verified for it.

providers.name: Lighthouse
providers.description: Lighthouse is an UNRESOLVED venture-portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network: the slug conflates at least two different companies named "Lighthouse" surfaced by two different VC portfolio harvests, and neither resolves to a live company with a developer surface. Accel lists Lighthouse as a seed-stage "metaverse search engine" at www.lighthouselabs.xyz — that domain now serves a GoDaddy/Afternic domain-for-sale parking lander (registered 2026-04-06, nameservers ns5/ns6.afternic.com), so the company appears defunct or renamed. DCM Ventures lists Lighthouse as an "AI meeting notes and productivity app" at lighthouse.app — that domain resolves 200 but serves an unrelated Texas apartment-rental cash-back platform transitioning to the UMoveFree brand, with no developer portal, no API, and no docs. The established hospitality/travel-intelligence company also named Lighthouse (formerly OTA Insight) is already profiled separately in the network as the lighthouse-travel provider and is NOT this record. Enrichment is blocked pending a human decision on which entity, if any, this slug should represent.

providers.name: Meet Cute

providers.description: LifeMed Media was a consumer health media company that operated dLife, a diabetes-focused media brand spanning dLife.com, the dLifeTV television program, the dLife Foundation, a diabetes retail store, and a section for healthcare professionals. Its editorial surface covered type 1, type 2, gestational and pre-diabetes, blood sugar management, insulin, complications, nutrition and recipes, and diabetes lifestyle content, monetized through sponsored sections from device and pharmaceutical advertisers. The company was venture backed by Battery Ventures. As of a 2026-07-19 verification pass the business appears defunct: its corporate domain lifemedmedia.com is parked for sale on HugeDomains and dlife.com no longer resolves. No developer portal, API, documentation, SDK, or other machine-readable surface has ever been identified for this company.
